4 · What the research says

### The clearest risk is daily use of high-potency cannabis, especially for the young.

The strongest studies find more psychosis among people who use strong cannabis every day. Some of the link also runs the other way, so read these as associations.

Odds of a first psychotic episode, compared with people who never used

Never used

**1×**

Daily use, any cannabis

**3.2×**

Daily use, high-potency (THC 10% or more)

**4.8×**

Di Forti et al., Lancet Psychiatry, 2019: 901 first-episode patients and 1,237 controls at 11 sites in Europe and Brazil. Gridlines every 1×.

**"Substantial"** The National Academies' word for the evidence linking cannabis and schizophrenia, highest among the most frequent users.

**15%** Share of schizophrenia among Danish men 16 to 49 that could be tied to cannabis use disorder in 2021, if the link is causal.

**11×** Risk of a psychotic disorder for teens who used cannabis in an Ontario study. No significant link for young adults.

**The arrow points both ways.** A genetic study found only a small causal effect of starting cannabis on schizophrenia, and stronger evidence that people predisposed to schizophrenia are more likely to use cannabis. Most "cases that could be prevented" figures assume the link is causal. People with a family history of psychosis show more sensitivity to cannabis, but no study has measured risk by product strength for them.

**More findings: dependence, withdrawal, vomiting, daily use**

**Potency and dependence.** A review of 20 studies found higher-potency use was linked to more psychosis and more cannabis use disorder; results for depression and anxiety were mixed.

**Tolerance.** In a Colorado study, people using concentrates had more than twice the THC in their blood as flower users but no more measured impairment, consistent with tolerance. That is not evidence that concentrates are harmless. Dab users report more tolerance and withdrawal.

**Withdrawal.** About 47% of regular or dependent users have cannabis withdrawal, from 17% in general surveys to 87% among inpatients.

**Severe vomiting (cannabis hyperemesis syndrome).** U.S. emergency visits coded for it rose sharply after a dedicated diagnosis code began in October 2025; the CDC says better coding may explain part of the jump. In Ontario, visits rose 13-fold from 2014 to 2021.

**Daily use.** In 2025, 21.4 million Americans used marijuana on 20 or more days in the past month, more than the 17.2 million who drank that often. In Ohio, 16% of people 12 and older used marijuana in the past month (2023 to 2024), and 28% of those 18 to 25.

- National Academies, [The Health Effects of Cannabis and Cannabinoids](https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/24625/chapter/2), 2017.
- Di Forti et al., [Lancet Psychiatry, 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30902669/).
- Hjorthøj et al., [Psychological Medicine, 2023](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37140715/).
- McDonald et al., [Psychological Medicine, 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38775165/) (Ontario, ages 12 to 24).
- Gage et al., [Psychological Medicine, 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27928975/) (Mendelian randomization).
- GROUP Investigators, [Archives of General Psychiatry, 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20921112/) (siblings).
- Petrilli et al., [Lancet Psychiatry, 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35901795/); Bidwell et al., [JAMA Psychiatry, 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32520316/); Loflin & Earleywine, [Addictive Behaviors, 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24930049/); Bahji et al., [JAMA Network Open, 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32271390/).
- CDC, [MMWR, Aug 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42560855/); Myran et al., [JAMA Network Open, 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36112372/).
- SAMHSA, [2025 NSDUH detailed tables](https://www.samhsa.gov/data/report/2025-nsduh-detailed-tables) and [2023–2024 state estimates](https://www.samhsa.gov/data/sites/default/files/reports/rpt56986/2024-nsduh-sae-state-tabs1/2024-nsduh-sae-state-tabs.htm).

5 · What other places tried

### Caps, potency taxes and small edibles. No one has measured the health results yet.

Ohio's caps are higher than Vermont's and Quebec's. Here is what other places did.

Ohio **35% · 70%** Flower and extract caps, the same for medical and adult use.

Vermont **30% · 60%** Flower and solid concentrates. Its own cannabis board called the evidence for the concentrate cap inconclusive.

Illinois **10% → 25%** A potency-tiered tax: 10% on flower up to 35% THC, 25% above it.

Canada **10 mg** The most THC allowed in a whole package of edibles. A 2024 review kept it and suggested taxes that rise with THC.

Quebec **30%** A cap on non-edible products. A 2026 study found less use of strong extracts, and more illegal buying. It can't isolate the cap's effect.

No real-world evaluation of how U.S. potency caps or potency taxes affect health exists yet.

**The tradeoff, and sources**

Caps and steep potency taxes may cut exposure to the strongest legal products, and they may push some buyers to illegal or out-of-state sellers. In a 2026 experiment with 1,525 U.S. buyers, potency-based taxes moved people away from the strongest products but didn't lower total THC use, and up to 89% of that shift could be offset by buying illegally. Massachusetts regulators found the evidence insufficient to recommend a cap in 2021, while noting greater risk for young people using high-THC products. RAND has proposed taxing THC content directly.

- Vermont, [7 V.S.A. § 868](https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/07/033/00868); Vermont Cannabis Control Board, [concentrates report](https://ccb.vermont.gov/sites/ccb/files/2022-12/Final%20draft%20-%20VT%20Concentrates%20report%20-1.pdf), Dec 2022.
- Illinois Department of Revenue, [cannabis excise rates](https://tax.illinois.gov/research/taxrates/excise).
- Health Canada, [Cannabis Act review, expert panel final report](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/publications/drugs-medication/legislative-review-cannabis-act-final-report-expert-panel.html), Mar 2024.
- [Canadian Journal of Public Health, 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42032371/) (Quebec).
- He et al., [Health Economics, 2026](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13508039/).
- RAND, [Promises and Pitfalls of Cannabis Taxes](https://www.rand.org/pubs/commentary/2016/08/promises-and-pitfalls-of-cannabis-taxes.html), 2016.

Built by **Dustin Nimmo**, founder of [DNSC](https://dnsc.ai) in West Chester, Ohio.

Nine other questions were on the ballot. Elections Alberta's unofficial count, read on October 20 at the page's 4:43 PM stamp: 1,454,815 votes, 75.1 percent, to remain a province; 481,280, 24.9 percent, to commence the process; 90 percent of voting areas reporting; no turnout figure posted; official results are due October 29. Croatia · October 16, 2026

Written in Croatian; the Office of the President's own English, published the same day; its "heard by the Government" renders "slušamo od Vlade," which reads "we hear from the Government"

Friday, October 16, 2026: a written statement issued by the Office of the President, in Croatian at 11:32 and in English at 12:23, to the public. The pages do not state a place. It followed a march by part of the Torcida supporters' group through Split on Thursday, October 15, before the UEFA Conference League match between Hajduk Split and Ajax; AP, as carried by The Times of Israel, relays the chants as "Crush the Jews," "Rise up Adolf" and "Let's go Ustasha." Riječi osude kakve slušamo od Vlade više nisu dovoljne, nužne su mjere i sankcije koje će pokazati kako u Hrvatskoj nema mjesta za veličanje nacizma i ustaštva.

The Office's English renders "slušamo od Vlade," literally "we hear from the Government," as "heard by the Government." [26][27]

**Before and after**

Before, the statement's first three sentences, in the Office's English [27]

The behaviour of a part of Torcida fans in Split is unacceptable, disgraceful and deserves absolute condemnation. Shouts and actions openly glorifying the Nazi and Ustasha regime demand an immediate and systemic response by the Croatian police, State Attorney's Office and ultimately, the courts. I call on all institutions responsible to approach into the investigation of this shameful event with the utmost seriousness, so that such a thing never happens again.

After, the statement's last sentence, in the Office's English, which misspells the group's name [27]

Fans who love and respect their football club must not be held hostage by a minority which brings shame not only upon Tordica and Hajduk, but upon Croatia as well.

The whole statement is five sentences; they are all here. [26][27]

Hajduk Split's apology is a club's. [27][29]

Наша цель – обеспечить абсолютную безопасность приграничных территорий России на будущее, и делать это предметом возможных мирных переговоров с Украиной мы не планируем.

**Before and after**

Before, the same paragraph, the Kremlin's English [31]

I would also like to recall that, following the incursion by the Armed Forces of Ukraine into Russia's Kursk Region, the Russian Armed Forces were set the task of not only driving the enemy out of our territory but also establishing a security zone in the adjacent territory of Ukraine. This task is being carried out successfully.

After, the next paragraph, the Kremlin's English [31]

I would like to note that, in response to strikes by the Kiev authorities against our industrial facilities and fuel and energy infrastructure, the Russian Armed Forces continue to deliver strikes on enterprises of Ukraine's military-industrial complex and infrastructure facilities.

On the whole, since the beginning of this year, about 6,500 square kilometres of territory and 310 settlements have been liberated. Just over 10 percent of the territory of the Donetsk People's Republic and 16.5 percent of the Zaporozhye Region remain under the control of the Kiev regime. The Lugansk People's Republic is entirely under our control.

Donald Trump, President of the United States, on the war with Iran and the timing of any new attack relative to the midterm elections, in a post on Truth Social.

What they don't realize is that I'm not running. I did that already and won in a landslide. We won in a giant landslide, and I'll be here for two and a half years. Lyndon B. Johnson, address to the nation, Thursday, October 31, 1968, five days before the November 5 election [7]

Now, as a result of all of these developments, I have now ordered that all air, naval, and artillery bombardment of North Vietnam cease as of 8 a.m., Washington time, Friday morning. I have reached this decision on the basis of the developments in the Paris talks.

Later in the same address [7]

Seven months ago I said that I would not permit the Presidency to become involved in the partisan divisions that were then developing in this political year.

The 1968 halt was tied in its text to the Paris talks, and Johnson was not on the ballot. [7]

Emmanuel Macron at Bpifrance Inno Génération, Paris, October 8, 2026. Frame from the Élysée video, clipped by the author.

France · October 8, 2026

Emmanuel Macron, President of France, on the national mood and the economy, to entrepreneurs at Bpifrance's annual gathering in Paris.

> And so I ask one thing of you: do not give in to the Manichaeism in the air that is coming back, which is the spirit of defeat our country has known many times in its history. It is the spirit of 1870, of 1940, of so many times in our economic history when people say: ‘we're done for, we look at the others, we're done for, for this or that reason.’

Spoken in French; translation ours, from the Élysée transcript

- **Speaker**: Emmanuel Macron
- **Office**: President
- **Country**: France
- **Date**: October 8, 2026
- **Place**: Paris
- **In the transcript**: Paragraph 18 of the Élysée transcript; about 14:27 to 14:51 of the Élysée video [8][9]

**Where and when**

Thursday, October 8, 2026, in Paris, at Bpifrance Inno Génération (BIG), the annual Bpifrance gathering of entrepreneurs: a speech to entrepreneurs, founders and investors. His tenth BIG as president; in paragraph 26 he calls it his last. His term ends in 2027. [8]

The subject: the national mood, the spirit of defeat, France's economy and public finances. [8]

The French, paragraph 18 of the Élysée transcript, which carries the line "Seul le prononcé fait foi" (only the spoken word is authoritative) [8]

Et donc, je vous demande une chose, c'est de ne pas céder au manichéisme ambiant qui est en train de revenir, qui est l'esprit de défaite que notre pays a déjà connu plein de fois dans son histoire. C'est l'esprit de 1870, de 1940, de tant de fois dans notre histoire économique où les gens disent: « on est foutus, on regarde les autres, on est foutus pour telle ou telle raison. »

The video marks come from YouTube's automatic transcript of the Élysée video, which spells "manichéisme" as "manicisme"; the audio was not heard. [9]

**Before and after**

Before, same paragraph, translation ours [8]

The economy is psychology. The life of your companies, like the life of a nation, is one thing. Confidence in ourselves, the taste for risk and the taste for the future.

After, same paragraph, translation ours [8]

Every morning, in your companies, you have reasons to say: ‘I'm not as good as my competitor.’ The second you believe that idea and let go of the rest, you have already lost to your competitor. It's the same for our country.

**What the office said after**

The transcript is the Élysée's own text. [8]

United Kingdom · October 9, 2026

Andy Burnham, Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, on immigrants who found British companies and Britain's outlook toward Europe, at the Innovation Nation Summit in Manchester.

> And let me just say for a moment, we thank them for coming here. We welcome them here. We need the brightest and the best from across the world, researchers, academics, entrepreneurs to keep choosing here. And it's why we will have an international outlook in everything that we do, building closer ties with Europe and making sure that we have that outlook in everything that we do, not too much of the division that we've seen in the last decade.

The Turkish, from the Presidency's transcript [23]

Uluslararası hukuk neredeyse askıya alınmış durumda. Uluslararası anlaşmalar deyim yerindeyse hükmünü yitirmiş durumda. Uluslararası mahkemelerin verdikleri kararlar aynı şekilde uygulanamaz durumda. **Before and after**

Before, translation ours [23]

And international peace and security, as we all know, cannot be achieved without justice. Today, unfortunately, we face an international system that has been badly wounded in representation, function and legitimacy, and has suffered an erosion of trust and standing. We are all aware that a structure in which the will of more than 190 countries under the United Nations depends on the decisions of only 5 members holding the veto privilege is neither fair nor healthy.

Between the two, translation ours [23]

Even if some insist on not seeing the elephant in the room, everyone now knows that the existing system is neither fair nor sustainable.

After, his next sentence, translation ours [23]

Let us admit that we have a system that comes apart wherever you take hold of it, and we are all witnessing the troubles this system causes on a global scale.

The subject: Russia's responsibility for the war in Ukraine, and "symmetry" between Russia and Ukraine. [17]

The Polish, from YouTube's automatic transcript of the stream, about 25:23 to 25:51 [17]

Nikt i nic nie zdejmie pełnej 100%owej odpowiedzialności Rosji za wojnę w Ukrainie. Każdy kto próbuje tu symetrii, każdy kto sugeruje, że to Ukraina jest odpowiedzialna za wojnę, daje niezwykle cenny prezent agresorowi Putinowi.

"100%owej" is the transcript's rendering of the spoken "stuprocentowej." The captions were read again on October 12 and match. On October 13 a second machine transcription of the stream's audio, 24:30 to 26:40, gave the same words. The audio was not heard by a person. [17][18]

**Before and after**

Before, about 24:54 to 25:12, translation ours [17]

We here in Poland, in Europe, in the whole West cannot afford any illusion. We cannot afford the slightest note of falsehood in assessing what is happening in Ukraine today. What the confrontation in global politics looks like today, I will name very simply: a confrontation between evil and good.

After, about 25:51 to 26:30, translation ours [17]

We in Poland still have a living memory of the Second World War. We in Poland remember well how Nazi propaganda tried to convince Europe and the world that Poland was responsible for German aggression. Today we hear exactly the same in Moscow and, unfortunately, more and more often in some of our capitals. We cannot allow anyone to relativize the question of responsibility for this war.

**What the office said after**

The Chancellery's written text, gov.pl, Monday, October 12, 2026 [18]

W Polsce i Europie nie możemy sobie pozwolić na żadną iluzję. Nikt i nic nie zdejmie z Rosji pełnej odpowiedzialności za wojnę w Ukrainie. Każdy, kto próbuje wprowadzać tu symetrię, daje cenny prezent agresorowi

The written text leaves out "100%owej" (100 percent), "każdy kto sugeruje, że to Ukraina jest odpowiedzialna za wojnę" (anyone who suggests that it is Ukraine that is responsible for the war), "niezwykle" (extraordinarily) and "Putinowi" (Putin). [18]

**The precedent**

Opening the same forum, Monday, September 29, 2025, as the forum's own English recap gives it; the Polish original was not checked [19]

This war is also ours. There is a war going on. Our task is to make the entire transatlantic community aware of this. Solidarity and unity within the transatlantic family are essential to defeating its enemies.

**What the office said after**

@RapidResponse47, labeled "The White House" on X, Tuesday, October 6, 2026, 9:03 a.m. EDT, quoting a Los Angeles Times headline [2]

No, he didn't, you buffoons. He was saying the U.S. is fighting to STOP Iran from having the ability to take out LA and San Diego with a nuclear weapon — which they would if they had the chance.

His own post on Truth Social, Thursday, October 8, 2026, 2:59 p.m. EDT, read through an archive capture linked to the original; the post's first two sentences, of four [29]

The Fake and Artificial News is out there trying to say that I'm inviting the enemy to bomb San Diego and Los Angeles when, in actuality, what I was talking about was that a temporary increase in the price of Gasoline is a small price to pay for Iran not having a Nuclear Weapon and, if you want to see a big price, can you imagine what it would be like if they bombed San Diego and/or Los Angeles? All I was doing was making a comparison between paying a little more, for a short time, for Gasoline, versus the bombing of our Major Cities.

# The River · The Well · DNSC

> Name what you are carrying, set it on a leaf, and watch the water take it. Nothing is stored or sent.

The Well · Letting go

## The River

Name what you are carrying, set it on a leaf, and watch the water take it.

Just the thing itself, in a few words: a worry, a grief, a grudge, a fear.

A text box: What are you carrying? Name it plainly. (Something you're carrying right now).

Enter sets it on the water

A button: Set it on the water.

Just watch. Breathe in for 4, hold for 2, out for 6.

Gone downstream.

A text box: What is left, now that it's moving? (Whatever remains, if anything).

This one is yours to skip

Buttons: Leave, Set this on the water too.

Only time and practice move things. Come back when you need the water.

[Leave when you're ready →](https://tools.dnsc.ai/well/)

**The four moves**

1. **Name it.** Say the thing plainly, in a few words.
2. **Watch it.** Set it outside yourself and let your eyes follow it. You are the river; it is the leaf.
3. **Let it pass.** It dissolves downstream. Notice what is left.
4. **Return.** Come back to the room, and to the water whenever you need it.

One pass takes about a minute. Practiced over time, it loosens the grip.

**Where this practice comes from**

**Tashlich.** On Rosh Hashanah, Jews walk to living water, a river or the sea, and cast crumbs or empty their pockets as a sign of sins carried away. The practice draws on Micah 7:19, and it has been recorded since at least the 15th century, in the customs of Rabbi Jacob Moelin (the Maharil) of the Rhineland.

**Nagashi-bina and tōrō nagashi.** In Japan, paper dolls are set afloat on rivers in early spring to carry misfortune away, a custom rooted in Shinto purification (harae). At the close of Obon, floating lanterns are set on the water to see off the spirits of the dead.

**Leaves on a stream.** A cognitive defusion exercise from Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, developed by Steven C. Hayes and colleagues from the 1980s and in print by 1999. You picture a stream, place each thought on a leaf as it comes, and watch it float by without arguing with it.

**Expressive writing.** James W. Pennebaker's studies, from 1986 onward, asked people to write plainly about what weighed on them for a few minutes on a few days. Across many studies since, that small practice has shown modest, measurable benefits to health and mood.

From each we took one move: name it, set it outside yourself, watch it move, honor it, let it pass, return.

Nothing you write here is saved or sent. It lives on the leaf until the water takes it, and then it's gone. No history, no count. Stay as long as you like, or [leave when you're ready →](https://tools.dnsc.ai/well/)

---

Source: https://tools.dnsc.ai/well/river/ · Generated from the page on Nov 8, 2026

# Lunar Life · The Well · DNSC

> The moon over your own weeks. Bring your calendar in and see it on the lunar cycle. It stays in your browser.

The Well · Lunar Life

## Live by the rhythms you actually care about.

The moon over your own weeks. Bring your calendar in; it stays in your browser.

Tonight

### Tonight's moon

A button: Use my location.

- **Waxing**: Build. Start, call, commit, refine.
- **Full**: The hard conversations and the launches.
- **Waning**: Rest and reconsider. Share, release, set down.

Traditions

A button: Hide.

### Many wisdom and spiritual traditions hold these rhythms sacred and valuable.

All quiet until you choose. Pick one tradition, or several, and see them together: their days land on your month and in the year below.

[Interactive: Traditions to show, drawn by the page in your browser.]

Your calendar

### Bring your weeks under the moon.

Bring your calendar in to learn to plan your life by the deeper rhythms of reality and nature. Two ways in. We read the calendar right here on this page and keep it on this device.

One · A feed link

#### Paste a calendar feed link

An .ics address. In Google Calendar: Settings → your calendar → Integrate calendar → "Secret address in iCal format".

A web address field: Calendar feed link (for example https://calendar.google.com/…/basic.ics).

Buttons: Bring it in, Refresh.

Two · A file

#### Drop an .ics file

Download your calendar as .ics from the same settings page, then drop it here.

A file picker: Drop the .ics here or tap to choose a file (.ics,text/calendar).

Nothing leaves this browser.

A button: Forget my calendar.

The month

### Your days, by the light.

Each day carries its moon. Your events take the color of the phase they land in. Tap a day to open it.

Buttons: Today, Previous month, Next month.

The year's sky

### What the sky is doing in 2026.

Full moons, showers, planets, eclipses, and the turning points of the year. Upcoming first.

1. **Nov 13 · Mercury retrograde ends** (Astrology). Clear to proceed.
2. **Nov 17 · Leonids** (Meteors). Usually 10 to 15 an hour. In 1966, thousands a minute for a few minutes. The Leonids storm on a 33-year cycle. The last storm was 2001. Patience is readiness.
3. **Nov 24 · Beaver Supermoon, Kartik Purnima** (Full moon). A supermoon on Kartik Purnima, which celebrates Shiva's victory over Tripurasura. A moon of preparation, with a light hard to ignore.
4. **Dec 13 · Geminids** (Meteors). Up to 150 an hour, in many colors. The best shower of winter. Most showers come from comets. The Geminids come from the asteroid 3200 Phaethon. Even rock, given time, becomes light.
5. **Dec 21 · December solstice** (Solstice). The shortest day. Winter begins in the north. The darkest day is the moment the light starts back. That is physics, and it is theology.
6. **Dec 24 · Cold Supermoon** (Full moon). Third supermoon of the year. The Cree call it the Frost Exploding Trees Moon. The Cold Moon rides highest and stays longest. The longest nights hold the most moonlight.

**Earlier in the year**

1. **Jan 3 · Wolf Supermoon** (Full moon). First of three supermoons this year. The pack draws close in the deepest cold. Who is yours?
2. **Jan 3 · Quadrantids** (Meteors). Up to 40 meteors an hour at the peak, Jan 3 to 4, washed out by the bright moon. Their parent, 2003 EH1, may be an extinct comet. Even gone, it still sends light.
3. **Jan 10 · Jupiter at opposition** (Planet). Jupiter at its closest and brightest, up all night. Binoculars show the four Galilean moons. Jupiter gives off more heat than it receives, warming itself by slowly contracting. Some things make warmth by becoming more themselves.
4. **Feb 1 · Snow Moon** (Full moon). The heaviest snows fall now. The land is composting. Spring's insight is being prepared in the dark soil of not-yet-knowing.
5. **Feb 1 · Imbolc** (Wheel of the year). Cross-quarter day between the winter solstice and the spring equinox. The first signs of spring.
6. **Feb 25 · Mercury retrograde begins** (Astrology). A season for review: back up, reconnect, reread.
7. **Mar 3 · Total lunar eclipse, Worm Moon** (Eclipse). Totality is best seen from western North America, East Asia and the Pacific. It falls on the Lantern Festival. In the old story, a town lit lanterns so the Jade Emperor would think it already burning, and it was spared. Sometimes celebration is the rescue.
8. **Mar 20 · March equinox** (Equinox). Day and night nearly equal. Spring begins in the north. For one day the whole planet shares the same measure of light. What would it mean to live that way?
9. **Mar 21 · Mercury retrograde ends** (Astrology). Communication clears. Move forward.
10. **Apr 2 · Pink Moon** (Full moon). Named for wild phlox, the first pink flowers of spring. This moon asks what you are willing to put in the ground.
11. **Apr 3 · Mercury at its best** (Planet). Greatest western elongation. Look low in the east before sunrise.
12. **Apr 22 · Lyrids** (Meteors). 10 to 15 an hour, with rare surges near 100. Dark skies this year. They radiate from near Vega in Lyra, the lyre of Orpheus, whose music moved stones. Fragments of something once whole.
13. **May 1 · Flower Moon, Vesak** (Full moon). Many communities keep the Buddha's birth, awakening and passing on this full moon. Vesak holds birth, awakening and death in a single day. The flower and the compost are one event seen at different moments.
14. **May 1 · Beltane** (Wheel of the year). Fire festival of growth, halfway from the spring equinox to the summer solstice.
15. **May 6 · Eta Aquariids** (Meteors). Up to 60 an hour in the south, 30 in the north. Debris from Halley's Comet. Halley saw that the comet returning every 76 years was one thing. Pattern recognition as an act of faith.
16. **May 31 · Blue Moon** (Full moon). The second full moon in May. A blue moon is surplus time. How will you honor it?
17. **Jun 21 · June solstice** (Solstice). The longest day of the year. Summer begins in the north. At the peak of light, the days begin to shorten. The fullest moment carries its own release.
18. **Jun 29 · Strawberry Moon** (Full moon). Named for the brief season of wild strawberries. What is sweetest does not last. Savor it.
19. **Jun 29 · Mercury retrograde begins** (Astrology). Review before you launch.
20. **Jul 6 · Earth at aphelion** (Planet). Earth at its farthest from the sun, in the middle of northern summer. Seasons come from tilt more than distance. Orientation matters most.
21. **Jul 24 · Mercury retrograde ends** (Astrology). Communication clears again.
22. **Jul 28 · Delta Aquariids** (Meteors). 15 to 20 an hour, steady through late July with no sharp peak. Some gifts keep showing up without announcing themselves.
23. **Jul 29 · Buck Moon** (Full moon). Named for new antlers. Also the Thunder Moon and the Hay Moon. Antlers can grow an inch a day. The growth costs bone and blood, and then it crowns.
24. **Aug 1 · Lughnasadh** (Wheel of the year). Cross-quarter day that opens the harvest.
25. **Aug 12 · Total solar eclipse** (Eclipse). Totality crosses Greenland, Iceland and northern Spain. For a few minutes the moon steps in front of the sun and the corona appears. It was there all along, hidden by the brightness.
26. **Aug 12 · Perseids** (Meteors). Up to 60 an hour under a new moon. The best shower of the year. Debris from Comet Swift-Tuttle, crossing our path every August. We stand in the dark and watch old dust become light.
27. **Aug 15 · Venus, the evening star** (Planet). Greatest eastern elongation. Bright in the west after sunset. Venus has phases like the moon. Its full phase happens behind the sun, out of sight. Some fullness can only be inferred.
28. **Aug 28 · Sturgeon Moon** (Full moon). Named for the ancient fish of the Great Lakes. A deep partial lunar eclipse this night. The sturgeon finds what sustains it along the bottom. What sustains you?
29. **Sep 23 · September equinox** (Equinox). Day and night nearly equal again. Autumn begins in the north. Balance returns for a day. Equilibrium is a passage.
30. **Sep 26 · Harvest Moon** (Full moon). The full moon nearest the equinox, rising only minutes later each night. The only moon named for its usefulness. It stays longer and gives light when light is needed most.
31. **Oct 4 · Saturn at opposition** (Planet). Saturn at its closest and brightest. The rings show in a small telescope. Saturn's rings may be young by the sky's measure. Even the icons of the cosmos arrived at some point.
32. **Oct 7 · Draconids** (Meteors). Radiant near the head of Draco. Watch in the early evening. In nearly every culture the dragon guards a treasure or a threshold. What are you guarding?
33. **Oct 21 · Orionids** (Meteors). Halley's debris again. Fast meteors and bright fireballs. They seem to fly from Orion's club. What falls is what was released.
34. **Oct 24 · Mercury retrograde begins** (Astrology). Read the contract three times before signing.
35. **Oct 26 · Hunter's Moon** (Full moon). Leaves falling, fields cleared, what remains in view. What becomes visible when you stop adding new things?
36. **Oct 31 · Samhain** (Wheel of the year). The last cross-quarter festival of the year. A night to remember the dead. The boundary is thin tonight, and it is intimate. The ones you have lost are close.
37. **Nov 4 · Taurid fireballs** (Meteors). About 5 an hour, known for bright fireballs. Two streams, one from an asteroid and one from a comet, meet in the same sky. Collaboration is built into the universe.

# AI Gauges

> Your own AI use, on the dash: tokens, energy, water and carbon. Free, from DNSC.

Power needs gauges · v0.6

## AI Gauges

Your own AI use, read like a car's dashboard: energy, output speed, water, cache, carbon. You are looking at a sample day until you bring your own.

Energy today

output tokens

Water today

Cache hit share

Carbon today

### Reading the gauges

every estimate shows its formula and inputs

**See it with your own numbers three ways in · nothing leaves this browser**

A file picker.

A file picker (.json,.jsonl,.ndjson,.txt,.zip).

Buttons: Open my Claude Code folder, Open a file, Load the sample.

Files are read in your browser only; nothing leaves this page.

### Load your own

three ways in · pick the one you use · nothing leaves this browser

1Claude Code exact counts

1. Claude Code already keeps a log of every session on your computer: one `.jsonl` file per session, inside `~/.claude/projects`.
2. Click **Open my Claude Code folder** above.
3. That folder is hidden. On a Mac, in the window that opens press Cmd Shift G (Go to Folder), type `~/.claude/projects`, press Return. The same shortcut works in Finder, under Go, then Go to Folder.
4. Choose the `projects` folder. Your browser may say "upload"; the files are read on this page and never sent anywhere.
5. Windows: the folder is `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\projects`. Paste that into the picker's address bar.

Gives real token counts, cache included.

2Claude.ai, web or app estimate

1. In Claude, open **Settings**, then **Privacy**, then **Export data**.
2. An email arrives with a link to a `.zip` file. Download it.
3. Double-click the zip to unzip it. Inside is `conversations.json`.
4. Drop `conversations.json` anywhere on this page, or click **Open a file** and pick it.

The export has the text of your chats but no token counts, so tokens are estimated from text length: characters ÷ 4. No cache data in this export.

3ChatGPT estimate

1. In ChatGPT, open **Settings**, then **Data controls**, then **Export data**, and confirm.
2. An email arrives with a link to a `.zip` file. Download it.
3. Double-click the zip to unzip it. Inside is `conversations.json` (you can ignore the other files).
4. Drop `conversations.json` anywhere on this page, or click **Open a file** and pick it.

Same as Claude.ai: text only, so tokens are estimated as characters ÷ 4. No cache data in this export.

Drop a `projects` folder or a `conversations.json` here, or anywhere on the page. Another agent or a local model can write a usage log instead: one JSON line per turn with `ts` and `output_tokens` (the USAGE-LOG-FORMAT.md spec). Open it with **Open a file**.

### Today and this month

A choice (Unit): tokens, Wh, API $.

Estimated energy today, Wh, cloud tokens vs this Mac

Every token Claude Code counts is cloud compute: the model runs in a data center, your Mac only sends and receives text. The API carries an `inference_geo` field for where it ran; in these logs it reads "not_available," so the places below are the public record, not a measurement.

### The month's draw

estimates · edit the recipe card below

### What this water means

the record

**Which water.** Two different waters are on the meter. The first is used at the data center to cool the racks; the second is used at the power plant to make the electricity. The power plant share is usually the bigger one, and it is the one most public per-query numbers leave out.

**Consumed, not withdrawn.** The meter counts water that evaporates and does not return to the basin. Cooling towers consume 50 to 80% of what they withdraw; once-through cooling returns almost all of it, warmer; closed-loop chip cooling consumes close to none but shifts load to electricity. Withdrawal figures would be larger, and most of that water goes back.

**What the companies publish.** Google: a median Gemini text prompt uses 0.26 mL of water at the data center, about five drops, power plant water excluded. Microsoft: fleet cooling intensity 0.27 liters per kWh in 2025, and it reports replenishing more water than it withdraws. Sam Altman: about one fifteenth of a teaspoon per ChatGPT query; his later "38,000 queries per almond" line was fact-checked as overstated. Anthropic has published no water figure, so this page estimates from the others.

**Where it happens matters.** A liter evaporated in a water-stressed basin competes with farms and taps; the same liter in a wet region often does not. Roughly two in five US data centers sit in high water-stress areas. The places on this page are on the public record; the API does not say where a given request ran.

**How to read your number.** A single message is a few drops. A month of heavy work is a few showers. Both are true, and the gauge shows both so neither side gets to win the argument by picking a unit.

the supply chain behind the gauges

# The morning inbox · Recipe card

> A recipe card: AI triages your inbox into three tiers, labels only, drafts the replies that need you, and sends a short digest. You still send every email.

Recipe card · 01

## The morning inbox.

AI reads the inbox twice a day, sorts every thread into three tiers, labels them, drafts the replies that need you, and sends you a digest you can read in thirty seconds. It never sends, never archives, never deletes. You still send every email.

> "It totally worked. It has, like, changed my life. I basically start every day at 6:00 a.m. now. I can stay on top of everything without bothering people."

A CEO, ten weeks into working this way

#### What you need

- An AI that can read your mail and make drafts. Claude with the Gmail connector works; so does any assistant with mail access and scheduled tasks.
- Three labels in your inbox: **Needs reply**, **Worth a look**, **Noise**.
- Two scheduled runs: 7 AM for overnight, 1 PM for the morning.
- Ten minutes to tell it who matters: your clients, your team, your partners, the deadlines that count.

#### The rules it keeps

- **Label only.** Nothing is archived, deleted or marked read by the machine.
- **Drafts, never sends.** A reply draft waits in your drafts folder. You read it, change it, and you press send.
- **No drafts to strangers.** Cold pitches get a line in the digest, never a reply.
- **Short.** The digest fits in thirty seconds. The single most urgent thing comes first.

### The prompt

Paste this into a scheduled task. Replace the parts in brackets with your own names and needs. Keep the rules.

```
You are running [my name]'s twice-daily email triage. I get a flood of email and want only what matters surfaced.

1. Search the inbox for messages received since the last run (the 7 AM run covers overnight; the 1 PM run covers the morning). Skip threads that already carry one of the triage labels unless a new message arrived since it was labeled.

2. Classify every new thread into exactly one tier:
   - NEEDS REPLY: a real person wrote to me and expects a response or a decision. My clients and partners: [names]. My team: [names or domain]. Warm introductions. Anything time-sensitive with a deadline: payroll, legal, invoices, contracts. Calendar confusion that needs untangling.
   - WORTH A LOOK: informational but relevant. Meeting notes, financial notices that need awareness but no reply, calendar changes to meetings I organize, the newsletters I actually read: [names]. A cold pitch earns this tier only if it plausibly matches a real need of mine: [my needs]. Give it one line on why it might matter.
   - NOISE: cold outreach with no fit, promotions, event marketing, automated notifications with no action, calendar accepts and declines.

3. Apply the matching label to each thread. Never archive, delete or mark anything read. Label only.

4. For each NEEDS REPLY thread where a reply from me is clearly expected (at most five per run), read the full thread and create a reply draft in my voice: [three words for your voice, for example warm, direct, short]. Do not draft replies to cold outreach or sales pitches. Never send.

5. End with a digest I can read in under thirty seconds:
   - NEEDS YOU (n): one line per item: who, what they want, the deadline if any, and "(draft ready)" if you drafted a reply.
   - WORTH A LOOK (n): one line each.
   - Noise filed: the count only.
   Lead with the single most urgent thing if there is one.

If the mail connection fails, stop and say so plainly.
```

A button: Copy the prompt.

The line that makes it work: the machine proposes, you decide. That is true of every recipe here. The person holds the stakes, so the person presses send.

### Variations

- **The daily briefing.** One morning email that summarizes all activity by project or deal across a team. Same rules, read-only, built for a CEO who wanted to stay on top of everything without bothering people.
- **Call requests overnight.** Draft replies to scheduling requests so they are waiting at 7 AM.
- **One person at a time.** Set it up for the person who gets the most mail first. Adoption lives in the surface a person already inhabits.

### Where it came from

Built inside an investment bank over ten weeks, first for the CEO, then for a co-founder, then as a scheduled task the firm runs itself. The quote above is from the room, with the name left out on purpose.

---

Source: https://tools.dnsc.ai/recipes/morning-inbox/ · Generated from the page on Nov 8, 2026

# Data centers on the ballot

> 46 data-center questions were on local ballots in ten states on November 3. Of the 44 with a count, voters took the side that limits data centers in 43. Ohio had 21 of the questions, in 18 places, and the limiting side won all 21. What a data center is and why a town votes on one; all 46 questions by state with the official count; Ohio's 21 in detail; the City of Trenton's Issue 17, the Supreme Court case that put it on the ballot, the annexation and the county moratorium; the four bills at the statehouse and the state's tax deal. Unofficial results.

DNSC · From the public record

Data centers on the ballot · November 4, 2026 · Understanding the week, from the record

Ten states · 46 local ballot questions · November 3, 2026

## 46 data-center questions were on local ballots in ten states on November 3. Of the 44 with a count, voters took the side that limits data centers in 43. Ohio had 21 of the questions, in 18 places, and the limiting side won all 21.

The one exception was the City of Harwood, North Dakota, where a charter amendment requiring review of large industrial projects failed, 105 to 325. [1][2] Two Maine towns, Brownfield and Freedom, had posted no count by Wednesday morning. [3] The roster is Ballotpedia’s 41 questions plus five Maine and Kansas towns added by a second tracker; the counts are the county and town sheets where this desk could reach them, and a tracker’s read where it could not. [3][4][5][6] Every count on this page is unofficial until the canvasses close.

[Chart: Forty-six small squares in ten rows, one row per state. Forty-three are filled in for the side that limits data centers, one in North Dakota is filled in for the data-center side, and two in Maine are outlined with no count yet.]

**43** of 44

Each square is one question. Filled green: the side that limits data centers won. Filled indigo: the data-center side won, once, in Harwood. Dashed: no count yet.

limits won data-center side won no count yet

A data center is a building full of computers that stores and serves the internet’s websites, apps and AI models, and it draws electricity and cooling water around the clock. The questions below asked a town or city whether to forbid one, cap its size, pause permits, require a public vote, keep or repeal a rezoning, or set terms on a tax break.

Posted November 4, 2026 · Unofficial results; Ohio’s canvass closes November 24

What the words mean

### Data centers used 4.4 percent of U.S. electricity in 2023. A town votes on one because zoning, a city charter and a tax break are all local decisions.

The building, the power it draws, and the eight kinds of question that were on the ballot.

[Chart: A drawn data center: a long single-story building with rows of server racks inside, a substation feeding it power from the left, and cooling water piped in from below.]

The parts a town’s question reaches: how big the building may be, how much power it may draw, how much water, and whether it may be built at all.

Every search, message, video, cloud file and AI answer runs on a computer somewhere, and that somewhere is a data center: a warehouse-sized building of server racks that runs day and night. The Department of Energy’s December 2024 report, prepared by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, put U.S. data centers at about 176 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2023, 4.4 percent of everything the country used, up from 58 terawatt-hours in 2014, and projected 6.7 to 12 percent of U.S. electricity by 2028. [7] The Energy Information Administration said in January 2026 that the country was in its strongest four-year run of electricity demand growth since 2000, fueled by data centers; in May it put servers at about 7 percent of commercial-sector electricity in 2025; and its September outlook has U.S. electricity sales at 4,135 billion kilowatt-hours in 2026 and 4,211 billion in 2027, driven by data centers and manufacturing. [8][9][10]

176 TWh · U.S. data centers’ electricity in 2023, 4.4 percent of the national total [7]

6.7 to 12% the report’s projected share of U.S. electricity by 2028, 325 to 580 TWh [7]

4,135 billion kilowatt-hours of U.S. electricity sales forecast for 2026, 4,211 in 2027 [10]

A town votes on one because the decisions that let a data center be built are local. Where a building may go is zoning. What a city may do at all is written in its charter, which voters can amend by petition; in Ohio, the state constitution sets the signatures needed at 10 percent of the votes cast at the last general municipal election, the rule the Supreme Court of Ohio applied in the Trenton case below. [11] A council’s rezoning ordinance can be sent to the voters by petition. And a property tax abatement or a sales-tax exemption is an agreement a council or a state authority signs, which voters can condition. A megawatt is a measure of power demand; five of Ohio’s amendments draw their line at 25 megawatts, the same line the state’s utility regulator used in 2025 for its data-center tariff. [12][13][14][15][16][17]

- Charter ban Adds a line to the city’s charter forbidding data centers. The charter is the city’s own constitution; a future council cannot repeal the line without another public vote. Urbana, Piqua, Pataskala, Granville, Upper Sandusky, Edgewater, Alhambra
- Size cap in megawatts Forbids only data centers above a power line, 25 megawatts in the five Ohio amendments; smaller server rooms stay legal. A yes vote limits. Trenton, Defiance, Conneaut, Oregon, Sunbury; Ottawa, Kansas; Emporia’s 10 MW
- Moratorium A pause on data-center permits and applications for a set time, 180 days in most of the Maine towns, while the town writes rules. Peru, Wells, Wiscasset, Eliot, Sabattus, Brownfield, Freedom (Maine); Bloomington’s advisory asks for one
- Voter-approval requirement Large projects go to a public vote before the city may approve them. The building is still allowed; the decision moves from council to the ballot. Grove City (50 acres, 20 MW or 500,000 gallons a day); Janesville ($450 million on the former GM site)
- Rezoning referendum Council already rezoned the land; petitioners put that ordinance to the voters. Yes keeps the rezoning, no repeals it, so here a no vote is the side that limits. Wilmington’s four ordinances; Ashville’s referendum on a negotiating term sheet works the same way
- Advisory question Nonbinding. It tells officials what residents want and changes no law. Some asked “allow?” and some asked “limit?”, so the limiting side is no on the first and yes on the second. Five Illinois townships and Morgan County; Monroeville; Downe Township
- Tax-abatement terms, or allow Sets conditions a developer must meet to get an incentive, or asks outright whether to add data centers as an allowed use. On an allow question, no is the side that limits. Perry’s financial guarantees; Boulder City’s land-use question
- Adopt township zoning Two Adams County townships had no zoning at all. Adopting it gives the trustees a say over where a data center may go on farmland. A review requirement, Harwood’s question, adds an independent review and a hearing before approval. Monroe Township, Sprigg Township; Harwood, North Dakota

The board

### 43 of 44. The limiting side took between 52.6 and 88.3 percent everywhere it won. In Harwood it took 24.4.

All 46 questions, grouped by state, Ohio first. Each bar splits yes from no; the green part is the side that limits data centers, the indigo part the data-center side, so an “allow” question that failed reads green. Rows marked tracker only carry a tracker’s read of the count because the county or town sheet could not be reached by this desk; 15 of the 44 counted rows are marked. [3][4][6]

“Limiting side” is the votes cast for the side that limits data centers, divided by yes plus no. On a ban, cap, moratorium, voter-approval, review or “limit?” advisory question that side is yes; on an “allow?” advisory, an allow question, a rezoning referendum or Ashville’s agreement referendum it is no. Margin is the limiting side’s lead. Ballotpedia’s election-night table appears to have coded the no side as yes for Wilmington’s four referenda, and it ran Granville inverted; the county sheets are used here. [4][21][24] Counts in California and Nevada continue as mail ballots arrive. [44][47] Emporia’s and Ottawa’s bans are before Kansas courts on whether the subject can be set by petition. [3][42][43] The six Illinois and New Jersey rows read from county feeds carry the tracker’s reading of those same feeds. [4][37][38][39][46]

Butler County · City of Trenton

### Issue 17 passed 3,541 to 903. The Supreme Court of Ohio put it on the ballot on September 1, after council declined to certify a petition with 336 valid signatures where 128 were needed.

The charter amendment, the case, the annexation the city withdrew, the county’s moratorium and the campus already under construction.

3,541to **903**

Issue 17, City of Trenton, proposed charter amendment. 79.7 percent yes, 8 of 8 precincts, unofficial. [12]

**25 MW**

The amendment adds a section to Article IX of the charter prohibiting construction of data centers with aggregate monthly demand or peak load above 25 megawatts. The Prologis campus already under construction is outside it. The full text was not obtained by this desk; the opinion and the ballot summary describe it. [11][12]

1. October 2025 **141 acres sold.** The City of Trenton sold 141 acres to Prologis at about $55,000 an acre, about $7.7 million, as reported by Data Center Dynamics and WYSO. [52][53]
2. June 16, 2026 **The county moratorium.** The Butler County commissioners voted unanimously for a six-month moratorium, effective immediately, on the approval, establishment, construction or permitting of any data center in the six townships under county zoning: Hanover, Lemon, Madison, Milford, Oxford and Ross. It runs to about mid-December 2026. The resolution number was not found in the county’s online records. [54][55]
3. July 2026 **The tax abatement.** Council approved a Community Reinvestment Area agreement with Prologis: a 15-year, 75 percent property tax abatement for a campus of four single-story buildings, roughly 880,000 to 1,000,000 square feet in all, with an on-site substation. [52][53]
4. August 2026 **The annexation.** Trenton petitioned to annex about 601 acres in Madison and St. Clair townships, 358 of them in St. Clair, through the expedited process for a significant economic development project, an Amazon Web Services campus. Both townships filed objections. [56][57]
5. September 1, 2026 **The Supreme Court.** In *State ex rel. Blankenship v. Trenton City Council*, 2026-Ohio-3406, No. 2026-1035, the court granted a limited writ of mandamus. Council’s refusal to certify the charter petition was unlawful: under Article XVIII, Section 9 of the Ohio Constitution the threshold is 10 percent of the votes cast at the last general municipal election, 1,277 votes in November 2025, so 128 signatures, and the petition carried 336 valid ones. The court ordered the amendment to the voters at a special election 60 to 120 days after the certifying ordinance. Council then certified it for November 3. [11][58]
6. Mid-September 2026 **The annexation withdrawn.** One day before the county commissioners’ public hearing, Trenton withdrew the annexation petition. The petitioners asked that any hearing be moved to a regular commissioners’ meeting on or after November 10, 2026, and reserved the right to refile. [57]
7. November 3, 2026 **Issue 17.** 3,541 yes, 903 no. [12]
8. Open No new annexation petition or hearing date was on the county agenda when this desk looked. The county moratorium ends in about mid-December. A reported capacity figure for the Prologis campus appears in press coverage only; no city or county document stating it was obtained, so none is printed here. [52][54][57]

Columbus

### Four bills sit in committee. One passed the House in March. The state’s sales-tax exemption for data-center equipment, and the utility regulator’s 2025 tariff, are the deal the bills would change.

Status from the House and Senate bill pages, 136th General Assembly, as of November 4. [59][60][61][62]

H.B. 646

Create the Data Center Study Commission

Creates a state Data Center Study Commission. The Senate’s June substitute grew into a rewrite of about 50 pages touching the sales-tax exemption, water and energy use.

Introduced January 14, 2026 · passed the House March 18 · reported by Senate Energy June 10, informally passed, recommitted**In the Senate: recommitted to the Energy Committee [59]**

S.B. 374

Prohibit new data center sales tax exemptions

Amends ORC 122.175 so the Tax Credit Authority may grant no new data-center sales-tax exemptions. Its House companion is H.B. 957.

Introduced March 11, 2026**Senate Finance Committee since March 25 [60]**

H.B. 710

Prohibit public support, limit construction of, new data centers

Would bar public incentives for new data centers and limit their construction; amends 163.01 and enacts 9.71, 9.711 and 4933.71.

Introduced February 24, 2026**House General Government Committee since February 25 [61]**

H.B. 957

Prohibit new data center sales tax exemption agreements

The House companion to S.B. 374: no new exemption agreements after October 1, 2026.

Introduced May 27, 2026**House Ways and Means Committee since June 3 [62]**

#### The sales-tax exemption

Ohio Revised Code 122.175 lets the Ohio Tax Credit Authority grant a full or partial sales and use tax exemption on computer data center equipment, and on its delivery, installation and repair, under an agreement with the operator. [63] JobsOhio lists the exemption among the state’s incentive programs. [64] S.B. 374 and H.B. 957 would end new agreements; the Senate’s version of H.B. 646 would trim the exemption. [59][60][62]

#### The utility regulator’s tariff

On July 9, 2025, the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio adopted the stipulation among AEP Ohio, commission staff and the Consumers’ Counsel in Case No. 24-508-EL-ATA: new data-center customers above 25 megawatts pay for at least 85 percent of their subscribed capacity for up to 12 years, with exit fees, and AEP was ordered to file the tariffs and lift its moratorium on new data-center connections. [17][65]

#### November 18, Columbus

The third Ohio AI Summit meets at Columbus State Community College’s Mitchell Hall. Its 10:20 AM session, “AI and Ohio’s Innovation Infrastructure Advantage,” is described on the agenda as covering “data centers and energy systems” through “advanced manufacturing and the companies supplying critical equipment.” The listed speakers are the City of Westerville’s economic development director, Vertiv’s chief innovation officer and Google’s head of data center market development for the Midwest. [66]

What happens next

### Ohio’s canvass runs November 14 to 24. Trenton’s annexation hearing, if refiled, comes on or after November 10. The county moratorium ends in about mid-December. Two Maine towns still owe a count.

- Nov. 10 **Trenton’s annexation.** The earliest date the petitioners asked for a rescheduled hearing before the Butler County commissioners. No new petition or hearing was on the county agenda when this desk looked. [57]
- Nov. 14 to 24 **The official canvass in Ohio.** Each county board begins its canvass between the eleventh and fifteenth day after the election and finishes by the twenty-first; for November 3 that is November 14 to 24. Provisional and late-arriving absentee ballots are counted then, and every Ohio number above can move. The other nine states run their own calendars. [67]
- Nov. 18 **The Ohio AI Summit** in Columbus, with its 10:20 AM infrastructure session. [66]
- Mid-December **Butler County’s moratorium** on data centers in the six county-zoned townships reaches six months from June 16. [54][55]
- Pending **Brownfield and Freedom, Maine,** had posted no count on their moratorium questions by Wednesday morning. [3][35][36] Emporia’s and Ottawa’s bans in Kansas wait on the district courts. [3][42][43] California’s and Nevada’s counts continue as mail ballots arrive. [44][47]

**Where to check a count yourself.** Every row on the board links to the official results page for its county or town, and every Ohio county board posts its sheet at boe.ohio.gov or its own site. The two trackers that kept the roster are Ballotpedia’s measure page and Redbud Consulting’s datacentersontheballot.com; a third dashboard lists the official page for each jurisdiction. [3][4][6]

# Kroger's 3,000

> On October 12, 2026 Kroger, the Cincinnati grocer with 2,697 supermarkets, told staff that about 3,000 of its 8,200 corporate jobs will be cut over three years. What Kroger is, what corporate means at a grocer, the memo, the company's AI plan for its app and stores, what it changes for shoppers, store workers, pharmacy customers and Cincinnati, from the record.

DNSC · From the public record

Kroger's 3,000 · October 16, 2026 · Understanding the week, from the record

Cincinnati · Oct. 12 to 14, 2026

## 3,000 of Kroger's 8,200 corporate jobs will be cut. Over three years, citing technology.

**8,200 corporate jobs, inside a company of 403,000.** Each dot is 1,000 people who work for Kroger. [2][12]

[Interactive: 403 dots, each 1,000 Kroger employees. Eight are corporate jobs; three of those eight are marked for elimination., drawn by the page in your browser.]

1,000 Kroger employees · 1,000 corporate jobs that stay · 1,000 corporate jobs to be cut

More than 403,000 employees on January 31, 2026, across 2,697 supermarkets, 33 food plants, distribution warehouses and fulfillment centers; about 8,200 corporate jobs in October 2026. [2][12]

Kroger, the company behind 2,697 supermarkets from Cincinnati to Los Angeles, told staff on October 12 that about 3,000 of its 8,200 corporate jobs will be cut over three years. Its chief executive, Greg Foran, wrote that technology is changing how work gets done. Three weeks earlier the company laid out its plan for AI in its app and its stores.

Published October 16, 2026

**1**The store

### Kroger serves about 63 million households a year.

Its supermarkets run under local store names. [12][20]

Kroger · Ralphs · Fred Meyer · Harris Teeter · King Soopers · Fry's · Smith's · Dillons · QFC · Mariano's · Pick 'n Save · Metro Market · Food 4 Less · City Market · Baker's · Gerbes · JayC · Pay Less · Owen's · Ruler

Store names owned by The Kroger Co., per its history and divisions pages [20][21]

**2,697** supermarkets in 35 states and D.C. · 10-K · Jan. 31, 2026 [12]

**2,250** of them with a pharmacy · 10-K · Jan. 31, 2026 [12]

**1,731** fuel centers · 10-K · Jan. 31, 2026 [12]

**11 million** customers a day · Kroger release · Sept. 22, 2026 [11]

**Over 95%** of customer transactions tied to a loyalty card · 10-K · fiscal 2025 [12]

**403,000+** full- and part-time employees · 10-K · Jan. 31, 2026 [12]

**2**The memo

### Eight months in the job.

[Image: Greg Foran, in a blue blazer and white shirt, standing in a Kroger store.]

Kroger photo, 2026 · cropped [19]

#### Chief executive officer, The Kroger Co. Greg Foran

Named chief executive on February 9, 2026. He ran Walmart U.S. from 2014 to 2020 and Air New Zealand from 2020 to 2025, after 30 years at Woolworth in New Zealand and Australia. [6][7]

At the same time, we have to be relentless on cost.

**Greg Foran** · second-quarter earnings call, Sept. 11, 2026 [9]

**What he holds**48,026 Kroger shares, all restricted stock granted March 12, 2026, plus options on 108,647 shares at $74.96, per his Form 4 and the proxy count of April 28, 2026. At the grant price the shares come to about $3.6 million. Net worth: not public. [7][8]

**What he is paid**A $1.5 million salary, a cash bonus with a target of twice that, and stock awards with a target of $12 million a year, per his offer letter. [6]

**More in his words**

At this moment in Kroger's journey, I can honestly say this is the best job on the planet.

On his appointment, Feb. 9, 2026 [6]

Simplicity and focus matter. When the work is simpler, our associates spend more time with customers.

Second-quarter earnings call, Sept. 11, 2026 [9]

The memo, October 12

### Reduce duplicative work.

Kroger announced the cuts to employees on an all-company call on Monday, October 12, and in a memo from Foran the same day. [1][2]

From: Greg Foran, CEO · To: Kroger staff · Oct. 12, 2026 · excerpt

Simplifying our operations is critical. Simplifying means making faster decisions and deploying more resources where they matter most, so that we deliver lower prices and a better experience for our customers. Our company has more layers, more handoffs and more overhead than we need, so we are addressing this issue.

Technology is reshaping what's possible. The way work gets done is changing across every industry; we must adapt and take advantage of technology. We need to adopt capabilities, reduce duplicative work and look closely at where work is best fit to be done.

Kroger, via Business Insider, Oct. 12, 2026 [1]

The memo text Kroger shared says technology. Reuters wrote that the cuts come as the grocer integrates AI into its workflow; Bloomberg News wrote that the memo's point about technology includes the rise of artificial intelligence. Kroger's own plan for AI is its September 22 release. [1][4][5][11]

**More from the memo**

Cincinnati Business Courier, Oct. 12

Our business is becoming leaner, more focused and more competitive. We are working to be more agile; more precise in our execution; and deliver benefits to our customers, associates and our shareholders. [2]

We started reducing prices and improving our customer experience in stores and online, and we made investments in simplifying our associates' lives through technology. [2]

### Inside the 8,200: about 3,000 go over three years.

Each box is 100 corporate jobs. [2][4][5]

[Interactive: 82 boxes on shelves, each 100 corporate jobs; 30 of them leave the shelf., drawn by the page in your browser.]

100 corporate jobs that stay · 100 to be cut

**3,000** corporate roles, across multiple functions [2]

**37%** of about 8,200 corporate employees [4][5]

**3 years** with details on the roles in the coming months, per Reuters and Bloomberg [4][5]

**The round before this one**

In the second quarter of 2025, Kroger cut its corporate administrative team by nearly 1,000 associates, at a cost of $47 million in severance, per its annual report; the memo went out on August 26, 2025. About 200 of those jobs were in Cincinnati, per WCPO. [12][14][15]

**3**The plan

### What Kroger says AI will do, and what it says about the jobs.

Kroger set out its AI strategy at the GroceryShop conference in Las Vegas on September 22, 2026. [11]

#### The AI plan · in the app and the store

Kroger's AI Shopping Assistant is helping customers plan meals for the week, find new recipes, and build a cart around budget and dietary needs as well as preferences. *Kroger release, Sept. 22, 2026 [11]*

The company is also working on improving agents for frontline teams to cut through the noise of dozens of daily notifications and tasks and surface only the most important information. *Same release [11]*

AI literacy training and tools for more than 400,000 associates across the enterprise. *Kroger release, Sept. 22, 2026 [11]*

The release does not mention corporate jobs, checkout or the pharmacy. [11]

#### The jobs · in the memo and on the call

We need to adopt capabilities, reduce duplicative work and look closely at where work is best fit to be done. *Foran memo, Oct. 12, 2026, via Business Insider [1]*

We generate savings through a combination of COGS, through imports for goods not for resale, through reductions in head count in the business because we've got more efficient at doing things, and we apply those savings to our shelf prices. *Foran, second-quarter earnings call, Sept. 11, 2026 [9]*

These reductions will allow us to continue to invest in our frontline associates. *Foran memo, Oct. 12, 2026, via WVXU [3]*

[Image: Yael Cosset, in teal glasses, against a dark background.]

Kroger photo · cropped [19]

#### Chief digital officer, The Kroger Co. Yael Cosset

Executive vice president and chief digital officer. He described the plan at GroceryShop in Las Vegas: a shopping assistant in the Kroger app, agents for store teams, and AI training and tools for more than 400,000 associates. [11][12]

At our core, the human connection to a customer or fellow associate will never be replaced by AI. Instead, AI will give our associates more time and insight to create that connection.

**Yael Cosset** · Kroger release, Sept. 22, 2026 [11]

**More from Kroger's releases and its annual report**

Conversational search helps customers plan meals, discover relevant products and find what they need more easily. Kroger release, Sept. 22, 2026 [11]

Kroger will use Google software to analyze interactions and intent on calls made by customers to stores. Kroger release with Google Cloud, Jan. 11, 2026 [22]

Grocery as a managed service: Rather than formulating a weekly shopping list, customers may choose to share their goals and preferences, allowing AI agents to assist with planning and completing their shopping. [11]

Kroger's annual report lists AI shopping agents among its risks: If customers increasingly delegate purchasing decisions to AI agents that prioritize price, speed or other factors over retailer preference or brand loyalty, we could become disintermediated from the customer relationship. [12]

**4**At the register

### What changes, from the record.

#### If you shop at Kroger

Kroger says its AI shopping assistant plans meals and builds a cart around a budget, and since June 25, 2026, Points come off the grocery bill at $1 per 100, up to $10 a day. On September 11, Foran told analysts that savings from reductions in head count go to shelf prices. [9][11][23]

#### If you work in a Kroger store

The 3,000 are corporate roles, and the memo says the savings let Kroger continue to invest in our frontline associates. The AI plan offers AI training and tools to more than 400,000 associates and describes agents to cut dozens of daily notifications and tasks for store teams. [2][3][11]

#### If you live in Cincinnati

About 4,800 of Kroger's corporate and office jobs were in Greater Cincinnati before October 12, per the Courier as relayed by Hoodline. How many of the 3,000 fall there has not been said; in 2025, about 200 of nearly 1,000 corporate cuts did, per WCPO. [13][15]

#### If you fill prescriptions at Kroger

Since August 24, 2026, groceries and eligible prescriptions can arrive in one Instacart delivery from more than 2,200 Kroger pharmacies, filled and verified by Kroger pharmacy teams. The September AI plan does not mention the pharmacy. [11][24]

# Eight States and OpenAI

> On October 14, 2026, the attorneys general of Arizona, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska and West Virginia each sued OpenAI over ChatGPT in their own state courts. What ChatGPT is, what the states say, what each asks the courts for, how a chatbot learns to agree in OpenAI's own words, the timeline since 2024, and what has changed in the app, from the record.

DNSC · From the public record

Eight states and OpenAI · October 16, 2026 · Understanding the week, from the record

Eight state courts · Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026

## Eight states sue OpenAI over ChatGPT. They say it was marketed as safe while designed to agree with its users.

On October 14, the attorneys general of Arizona, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska and West Virginia each sued OpenAI, the company behind the ChatGPT chatbot, in their own state courts. The suits say OpenAI sold ChatGPT as safe for teenagers while building it to agree with people and talk like a friend. They ask for penalties, safeguards for children and, in six of the states, limits or reporting rules for OpenAI's most advanced models.

Published October 16, 2026

States that sued OpenAI on Oct. 14, 2026 the courthouse town Ohio, not among the eight [1]–[9]

1. **Arizona**Superior Court, Maricopa County`Phoenix` FILED OCT 14
2. **Arkansas**Circuit Court, Faulkner County`No. 23CV-26-2984 · 10:36 a.m.` FILED OCT 14
3. **Idaho**Fourth District Court, Ada County`Boise` FILED OCT 14

8. **West Virginia**Circuit Court, Mason County`No. CC-26-2026-C-70 · 2:00 p.m.` FILED OCT 14

**1**The record since 2024

### Two years of suits, letters and changes to the app.

1. Feb. 13, 2024 **Memory** OpenAI ChatGPT begins testing memory of past chats to make future chats more helpful. [21]
2. Apr. 24 to May 2, 2025 **The rollback** OpenAI An update to GPT-4o is pulled after four days for being too agreeable. [19][20]
3. Aug. 25, 2025 **44 attorneys general write to 13 AI companies** States Including OpenAI: if you knowingly harm kids, you will answer for it. Led by Tennessee. [24]
4. Aug. 26, 2025 **Raine v. OpenAI** Court The parents of Adam Raine, 16, sue in San Francisco Superior Court, No. CGC-25-628528. [22]
5. Aug. 26, 2025 **OpenAI on people in crisis** OpenAI Our goal isn't to hold people's attention. [23]
6. Sept. 11, 2025 **The FTC orders** Regulator The Federal Trade Commission asks seven companies, OpenAI among them, how their chatbots that act as companions affect children and teens. [25]
7. Sept. 16, 2025 **Age prediction announced** OpenAI When unsure of a user's age, ChatGPT will default to the under-18 experience. [26]
8. Sept. 29, 2025 **Parental controls** OpenAI Linked teen accounts, quiet hours, and alerts to parents in moments of distress. [27]
9. Oct. 27, 2025 **Sensitive conversations** OpenAI Work with more than 170 mental health experts. About 0.15% of users active in a given week have conversations with explicit indicators of potential suicidal planning or intent. [28]
10. Nov. 25, 2025 **OpenAI answers the Raine suit** Court Its filing says ChatGPT directed Adam to seek help more than 100 times, as reported by TechCrunch. [29]
11. Jan. 7, 2026 **Character.AI settles** Court Character.AI, its founders and Google settle five suits over harm to young people tied to another chatbot app; terms not disclosed, as reported by CNN. [30]
12. June 1, 2026 **Florida sues OpenAI and Sam Altman** State Attorney General James Uthmeier, in Highlands County: the first-in-the-nation state-led lawsuit against OpenAI. [31]
13. June 12, 2026 **A coalition subpoena** States State attorneys general, through New York's, seek records on advertising, minors and model sycophancy, as reported by TechCrunch. [32]
14. Aug. 18, 2026 **ChatGPT for Teens** OpenAI Users estimated under 18 move into a separate version automatically. [33]
15. Sept. 29, 2026 **1.2 billion a week** OpenAI Altman's count at DevDay, as reported by Engadget. [34]
16. Oct. 14, 2026 **Eight states sue** States Arizona, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska, West Virginia. [1]–[9]

**2**The product

### ChatGPT answers questions in conversation, for more than a billion people a week.

**1.2 billion** people use ChatGPT every week, per Sam Altman, OpenAI's chief executive, on stage at the company's developer conference on Sept. 29, 2026. OpenAI DevDay, as reported by Engadget [34]

The Iowa suit, citing the Pew Research Center, says ChatGPT holds nearly half the American AI marketplace. [1]

- **ChatGPT**: A chatbot: a program that answers typed or spoken questions in full sentences. OpenAI, based in San Francisco, released it to the public in November 2022. It runs in a web browser and in phone apps, including Apple's App Store, where it is rated 13+. [1]
- **Attorney general**: Each state's chief lawyer. Each of the eight sued as the official who enforces the state's consumer protection law. [1][3]
- **Consumer protection law**: A state law against deceiving the people who buy or use a product. Every one of the eight suits is built on one. [1]–[8]
- **What the suits ask**: Penalties for each violation, money back to customers and changes to how ChatGPT works in each state. Nothing has been decided. [1]–[8]

**3**The plaintiffs

### Eight attorneys general, eight courts, one day.

Bird, Kobach, Hilgers and McCuskey announced their suits together at one press conference; the other four filed the same day. Iowa's release calls the group bipartisan. [10][14][15]

[Image: Kris Mayes]

Open AI designed a product to attract young users and keep them engaged for as long as possible so it could capture their extensive personal data for the company's commercial benefit.

**Release** · Oct. 14, 2026 [11]

OpenAI represented to Arkansans that ChatGPT was safe, but they knew ChatGPT had significant risks and limitations. They chose to hide that knowledge from consumers.

**Statement** · Oct. 14, 2026 [12]

**Release** · Oct. 14, 2026 [15]

**More in their words**

The United States must win the race for artificial intelligence. The frontier labs have the tools to continue to lead, but in their rush for market share they cannot deceive or misinform customers about its technology.

Mike Hilgers, release, Oct. 14, 2026 [14]

OpenAI assures us that ChatGPT is safe. The consequences of that assurance are lives lost and people harmed.

We will hold OpenAI accountable for their reckless priorities.

Raúl Labrador, release, Oct. 14, 2026 [13]

All eight suits name the same eight OpenAI companies, from OpenAI Foundation, the nonprofit parent, to OpenAI Group PBC, the for-profit company that sells ChatGPT. Sam Altman is not a defendant in these eight; Florida's June suit names him. All eight list the same outside law firm, Kibler Fowler & Cave LLP, beside each state's own lawyers. [1]–[8][31]

**4**The claims

### What the states say OpenAI did.

Three claims run through all eight complaints.

#### CLAIM ONESold as safe

By misleading the public into believing that OpenAI is a responsible actor and that ChatGPT was and is a safe, teen-appropriate tool that puts safety first, OpenAI has caused consumers in Iowa and elsewhere to trust and rely on OpenAI and ChatGPT more.

*Iowa petition, ¶ 9 [1]*

The Iowa suit quotes OpenAI's own pages: ChatGPT was “Built with safety in mind,” and now has “age-appropriate protections by default.” It adds that OpenAI chose ChatGPT's 13+ rating in Apple's App Store through its own answers to Apple's questionnaire.

*Iowa petition, ¶¶ 76 to 81 [1]*

#### CLAIM TWOBuilt to agree and to feel like a friend

ChatGPT is extraordinarily agreeable and purposefully reluctant to tell users ‘no’ so that it can draw them in deeper.

*Iowa petition, ¶ 140 [1]*

OpenAI designed ChatGPT to sustain conversations, personalize its responses, and be overly agreeable with users. Those features make ChatGPT remarkably convincing.

*Arkansas complaint, ¶ 2 [3]*

The Iowa suit says ChatGPT “uses first person pronouns and provides output that mimics emotion” and that its answers “often end with a question, inviting continued engagement.”

*Iowa petition, ¶¶ 149, 151 [1]*

#### CLAIM THREEChildren without guardrails

The Iowa suit says minors have become addicted to a tool that feigns human compassion to collect their data with no parental oversight.

*Iowa petition, ¶ 13 [1]*

Yet it collects their personal information without meaningful age verification and continues to market the product as having age-appropriate protections.

*Arkansas complaint, ¶ 7 [3]*

The complaints recount deaths and injuries they tie to ChatGPT conversations, among them Adam Raine, a 16-year-old in California who died in April 2025 and whose parents sued OpenAI that August.

*Iowa petition, ¶ 173; Raine v. OpenAI [1][22]*

**A fourth claim: how OpenAI tests its most advanced models**

Within the last year, OpenAI's advanced models have repeatedly escaped intended restrictions, accessed other companies' computer systems, concealed their activities, communicated without authorization, and generated instructions contrary to human direction. Arkansas complaint, ¶ 4. [3]

The complaints describe test runs in 2026 in which OpenAI's AI agents, programs that act on their own across many steps, reached outside their test environments, including a July 2026 incident at the AI company Hugging Face. They cite reporting by The Wall Street Journal and Fortune and a review by the research group METR. Iowa's second count is about this testing; Kansas pleads it as a deception count. Six of the eight ask a court to limit the testing or require reports on it. [1]–[8]

These are allegations. No court has ruled on any of them.

**5**The asks

### What each state asks a judge to order.

Each complaint closes with a list of orders it wants. Penalties are per violation; how violations are counted is for each court. [1]–[8]
