# Who guards the pipes

> The Ohio Auditor of State's web server was attacked on Sunday, October 25, 2026, and the office that audits every local government in Ohio took its site offline. What the office has said, what it has not, the county that lost its own property search for days in 2024, the state's count of more than 150 local cyber incidents, the law that now requires a cyber program in every county and seals the record, what Ohio built before the attacks, the federal program that lost its funding, the vendors underneath, and what is and is not known about how attacks get in. From the record, October 2026.

DNSC · From the public record

Who guards the pipes · October 27, 2026 · Understanding the week, from the record

Ohio · Butler County · Oct. 25 to 27, 2026

## The office that audits every local government in Ohio went offline Sunday. The counties it audits run on the same kinds of vendor systems, and the state counts more than 150 local cyber incidents in three years.

The Ohio Auditor of State audits every county, city, village, township and school district in the state. On Sunday, October 25, its web server was attacked, and the office took the server and its online accounts offline. [1][2] In January the same office said it had logged more than 150 cyber incidents at Ohio local governments in three years, with losses up to $1.9 million. [3] Since January 1 state law has required every county and city to have a cybersecurity program, and the same law seals the record of it. [14][15]

[Chart: A drawn diagram: one state office at the top, a row of 88 county offices below it, and a row of vendor systems underneath the counties. The state office is marked offline.]

150+

cyber incidents at Ohio local governments in three years, by the Auditor of State’s own count in January 2026. Losses ran from a few thousand dollars to $1.9 million. [3]

Most of the money, the office said then, left through schemes that redirect a vendor payment. [3]

In April 2024 the Butler County Auditor’s own property search went dark for days, and the office said, All we really know is what Tyler is telling us. [4] Three of the seven systems behind that office today are hosted by the same vendor. [31]

Posted October 27, 2026

What happened this week

### The state’s web server went offline Sunday. The office says the data is intact. The method is not public.

- Sun. Oct. 25 The Auditor of State’s web server is attacked. The office later said its threat monitoring systems detected and quarantined the intrusion, and that it then disconnected the web server and its online accounts, as WHIO reported. [2]
- Tue. Oct. 27 The office’s statement, as reported by WOSU: the server was attacked by overseas cybercriminals and potentially foreign state actors. It is not a ransomware attack. The office still has all the data it did before the attack. It said it had no evidence that Ohioans’ personal financial information was put at risk, and no reason to believe that audited entities’ financial information was. [1] > Out of an abundance of caution, we took the web server and online accounts offline while internal and external experts scrutinize the threat activity. > > We quickly notified state and federal law enforcement and are working closely with them to identify the cybercriminals involved. > > Auditor of State Keith Faber, statement of Oct. 27, 2026, as quoted by WOSU [1] Payments to the office run through a separate state portal and are not stored on the web server; the office set a grace period for payments until further notice. It plans a temporary web platform while the permanent server is down. [2] It said it would tell the public more about this when we know more. [1]
- Tue. evening ohioauditor.gov did not answer when this page was built; the connection timed out. The office’s cybersecurity-program page and its Bulletin 2025-007, the state’s guidance to local governments under the new law, sit on that server. [31]

Not on the record

How the attackers got in. Who they were, beyond the office’s description. Whether anything left the server. How long the site will be down. Whether any audited entity missed an online filing or payment. Whether the office’s own cybersecurity program, the kind the new law requires of local governments, was tested before Sunday. The office has said it will say more when it knows more. [1]

The record closer to home

### Butler County’s property search went dark for days in April 2024. Its cities and townships have had incidents this year. Five other counties have too.

#### The Butler County Auditor, 2024

- Sun. Apr. 14, 2024 Tyler Technologies, which hosted the auditor’s property-search site, reported unusual activity in the public-facing property access hosting environment and took the site offline as a precaution. It stayed down through at least Wednesday, April 17. The office said the problem was limited to the website software, and told residents to paste a backup link into a browser to reach property records. [4] > All we really know is what Tyler is telling us. > > Butler County Auditor Nancy Nix, to the Journal-News, April 16, 2024 [4] A follow-up in the Journal-News said the office reported no sign of attack or malicious activity, just some unusual activity (multiple repeating hits to the website). Real Estate Search came back first. [5]
- Late May 2024 A new site, built by Revize, goes live at auditor.bcohio.gov about six weeks after the unusual activity, as the Journal-News reported. Property data stays on Tyler’s iasWorld Public Access. The cost of the rebuild is not in the coverage. [6]

#### Butler County’s cities and townships

From a Journal-News story carried by WCPO, undated on WCPO’s page; its officials speak of incidents this year. [7]

- **Liberty Township.** A cyber incident in May. The board later adopted a cybersecurity policy that formalized some of the lessons learned from the May cyber incident. [7]
- **West Chester Township.** Two incidents this year. The township’s spokesperson: It was the same group, so it was more like a combined incident. [7]
- **Middletown.** An August incident affected staff email, access to records and phone records. The city spent $295,000 on technology upgrades afterward. [7]
- **Hamilton.** Contracted with Secure Cyber of Moraine in 2019 after a minor incident; no incidents reported since. [7]

#### The county’s program, Dec. 16, 2025

Butler County commissioners were presented the county cybersecurity program the new state law requires, for adoption before January 1, 2026. The full plan is exempt from public records; an executive summary was provided, as summarized by Citizen Portal from the meeting. [8]

Whether that program covers the county’s separately elected offices, the Auditor among them, or only the departments under the commissioners, is not in the public summary. [8]

#### Other Ohio counties, December 2024 to March 2026

| When | County | What the record says |
|---|---|---|
| Dec. 2024 | Wood | Ransomware detected Dec. 9. On Dec. 23 the commissioners said the county had negotiated and paid $1.5 million to resolve it, from reserve funds, on the advice of outside forensic consultants. [9] |
| May 6 to 18, 2025 | Union | Ransomware. The county’s notice says the intruders were in its network from May 6 to May 18 and took data on 45,487 people, including Social Security and driver’s license numbers. Notices went out Sept. 24, 2025. [10] |
| Late May 2025 | Lorain | A network security incident closed the Court of Common Pleas, Domestic Relations and Juvenile Court and Adult Probation while systems were offline; 911 stayed up. Services resumed within about a week. [11] |
| Nov. 2025 | Trumbull | County officials said an attempted attack came through a third-party vendor’s breach and reached the Recorder’s office; they said county IT staff and an outside firm stopped it without data loss. [12] |
| Mar. 15 to 17, 2026 | Lucas | A security incident. The Auditor’s Real Estate Information System was down from at least Sunday until after 8 PM Tuesday; the dog-licensing portal was down Tuesday. The county: we took certain systems offline out of an abundance of caution. [13] |

Each row is from the county’s own notice or local reporting, linked in the sources. Incident reports filed with the state under the new law are not public records, so this table is what the counties and the press have said in public. [14]

The count

### The state logs the schemes and the dollars. It publishes no AI share.

The only Ohio-specific count on the record is the Auditor of State’s. The rising-trend and AI figures below come from security companies’ surveys and research, and are labeled as such.

150incidents, three years

The Auditor of State’s office told the Statehouse News Bureau in January 2026 that it had logged more than 150 cybercrime incidents at local governments over the past three years, at counties, cities, townships, villages and school districts, with losses from a few thousand dollars to $1.9 million. The schemes it named: ransomware and business email compromise that redirects a vendor payment. [3]

> I’ll be blunt; I think we lose more money to cyber fraud in Ohio than we do to employee theft and dishonesty, which is a big statement.
>
> Auditor of State Keith Faber, to the Statehouse News Bureau, Jan. 20, 2026 [3]

None of the state’s public statements, in January or this week, gives a count of incidents that involved AI, or says whether the office tracks that. [1][3]

Vendor research

65percent rise

Trend Micro’s threat intelligence for the first quarter of 2026 says the first half of 2025 saw a 65% year-over-year increase in ransomware incidents affecting government bodies (208 confirmed attacks), a trajectory that continues in 2026. The same report says ransomware groups are now deploying AI to autonomously handle reconnaissance, a statement about attackers generally. The count is national. [16]

Industry survey

84percent of victims

Semperis, a security company, polled 1,200 IT and security professionals in nine countries for its 2026 Ransomware Risk Report. Among those whose organizations were hit, 84 percent said AI was used in the attack, as CBS News reported on Oct. 14, 2026. A survey asks victims what they believe; it does not inspect the attacks. [17][18]

Industry survey

65percent of victims

Proofpoint’s 2026 AI-Era Ransomware Report, July 21, 2026, from a global survey of security professionals, says 65 percent of ransomware victims confirmed AI use made the attack more effective. The report page does not say how many people were surveyed. [19]

What the law requires

### Since September 30, 2025, every political subdivision must have a cyber program and report every incident. The records are sealed.

House Bill 96, the state operating budget for fiscal years 2026 and 2027, was signed June 30, 2025 and took effect September 30, 2025. It added section 9.64 to the Ohio Revised Code. The Journal-News calls it a non-funded mandate. [7][14]

#### What R.C. 9.64 requires

- **A cybersecurity program** in every political subdivision, covering risk identification, impact identification, threat detection, incident response, post-incident security and employee training. [14]
- **Deadlines.** Counties and cities by January 1, 2026; other subdivisions by July 1, 2026, per the County Commissioners Association’s bulletin. [15]
- **Reporting.** After a cybersecurity or ransomware incident: notify the Ohio Division of Homeland Security within seven days and the Auditor of State within thirty. [14]
- **Ransom.** No payment unless the legislative authority approves it via resolution or ordinance. [14]

#### What the public can read

- The program itself and incident reports are not public records. [14]
- Procurement records that identify cybersecurity software, hardware or services are classified as security records. [14]
- What remains public: what each office chooses to say, and when, as it did in Butler County in April 2024 and at the state this week. [1][4]
- The Auditor of State’s own guidance under the law, Bulletin 2025-007 and its cybersecurity-program page, is on the server that is offline. [31]

What was built before the attacks

### Ohio has a volunteer cyber reserve, a free training program for local governments, and a center that coordinates incident response.

#### The Ohio Cyber Reserve, 2019

Created by Senate Bill 52, signed by Gov. Mike DeWine on October 25, 2019: a volunteer cyber force under the direction and supervision of the Adjutant General’s Department, made up of trained, vetted Ohio civilians working from Ohio National Guard readiness centers in five regions. Its stated jobs: help small municipalities test their systems for vulnerabilities, respond to attacks on eligible local governments, and teach. [20]

The first eleven members finished the state’s assessment course in October 2021, the Guard reported that November; the reserve then had about 50 members in Cleveland, Columbus and Cincinnati. [21] By December 2024 the governor’s cybersecurity adviser counted 177 reservists and expected 200 by year’s end. His slide: The Cyber Reserve is not formulated to be the first line of defense. [22] Its mission statement today: Assist, Educate, and Respond as directed by the governor and the adjutant general. [23]

#### Training at no cost, and a response center

**Ohio Persistent Cyber Improvement.** A local-government training and assessment program run through the University of Cincinnati’s Ohio Cyber Range Institute, delivered at no cost to Ohio-based Local Government Entities and funded through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and the State of Ohio. The December 4, 2024 deck counted over 1,797 local public employees currently receiving training in 5 counties and 42 local entities in 25 counties in the pipeline. Butler is on its 2025 list, with Athens, Cuyahoga, Hamilton, Mahoning and Clermont among others. [22]

**The Ohio Cyber Integration Center.** A fusion center that shares cyber intelligence and coordinates incident response for local governments, under Ohio Homeland Security; the deck said it formally opens in 2025 with a planned staff of ten. The Cyber Reserve’s own site sends any organization with an incident to the center first. [22][23]

What was taken away

### The federal information-sharing center that about 19,000 local governments used lost its funding in 2025.

- **March 2025.** CISA cut federal funding for the Multi-State Information Sharing and Analysis Center, run by the Center for Internet Security. The size of the cut differs by source: $10 million, just under half of the MS-ISAC’s funding, per the National Association of Counties; $8.3 million, more than half of the program’s remaining 2025 budget, per Smart Cities Dive citing CIS. Smart Cities Dive put the center’s fiscal 2025 operating budget at $27 million. [24][25]
- **Who used it.** More than 17,000 state, local, tribal and territorial entities, per NACo in March; more than 18,000 served, per Smart Cities Dive in August; close to 19,000 members before the cuts, per Cybersecurity Dive in October. The center detected more than 43,000 potential attacks on state and local governments in 2024, Smart Cities Dive reported. [24][25][27]
- **Aug. 7, 2025.** The U.S. Conference of Mayors, the National League of Cities, NACo, the state CIOs’ association and the Major County Sheriffs of America asked Congress to restore the money: The loss of federal funding will create significant vulnerabilities for rural and small communities. [25]
- **August 2025.** The federal government barred recipients of State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program funds from spending them on MS-ISAC memberships, Cybersecurity Dive reported. [27]
- **Sept. 30, 2025.** The cooperative agreement between CISA and CIS ended with the fiscal year; Cybersecurity Dive described it as a $48.5 million annual agreement. CIS said it needed $1+ million per month to keep the services running and would move to a membership model; its lowest tier rises to $1,495 a year. [26][27]

> The MS-ISAC, operated by CIS, has been this nation’s most successful public-private partnership.
>
> John Gilligan, president and chief executive of the Center for Internet Security, Sept. 2025, as quoted by Help Net Security [26]

**What Ohio has said.** Nothing on the record from the Auditor of State, the Ohio Cyber Integration Center or the governor’s office addresses how many Ohio local governments belonged to MS-ISAC, or how many have paid to stay. That is a question for the record, and this page does not guess at it.

The vendor layer

### Seven systems hold the Butler County Auditor’s public work. Three are Tyler Technologies. Tyler had its own ransomware attack in 2020.

Read from the live site and its response headers on October 5 and October 27, 2026. [31]

| System | Vendor | What lives there |
|---|---|---|
| auditor.bcohio.gov | Revize, on Amazon’s cloud | The pages. Page addresses end in .php. The footer reads Powered by revize and © 2024, with news items through September 2026. [31] |
| propertysearch.bcohio.gov | Tyler Technologies iasWorld | Every parcel value, the 2026 reappraisal, CAUV and homestead flags. The system that went dark in April 2024. [4][31] |
| ess.bcohio.gov | Tyler Munis | County finance: payroll and budget; the ledger inferred from the product. [31] |
| butlerohsmartfile.tylerhost.net | Tyler SmartFile | Online filings, Board of Revision complaints. [31] |
| gismaps.bceo.org | Esri ArcGIS, County Engineer | Parcel maps. [31] |
| butlercountyohio.docupet.com | DocuPet | Dog licenses. [31] |
| files.bcohio.gov | Nextcloud, self-hosted | Forms and downloads. [31] |

The auditor’s office does not take payments on its own site; those sit with the county Treasurer. No privacy or security statement appears on auditor.bcohio.gov. [31]

#### Tyler Technologies, September 2020

On September 23, 2020 Tyler told clients an unauthorized intruder had disrupted access to some of our internal systems, and that it had no reason to believe that any client data, client servers, or hosted systems were affected, as StateScoop reported. [28] Two days later the company confirmed to the Associated Press that the intruder used ransomware; it said the impact appeared limited and a spokesperson did not directly answer a question about whether it paid. [30]

NBC News reported that several counties using Tyler’s software said they had seen evidence they were affected with ransomware. Tyler serves dozens of counties and cities across the country. [29]

#### What that record shows, and what it does not

A vendor that hosts a county’s records can be attacked on its own corporate network, and the county learns what the vendor tells it: that was Tyler’s account in 2020 and Butler County’s experience in 2024. [4][28]

No source connects the 2020 Tyler attack to Butler County, and no source connects any vendor to the attack on the state’s server this week. The state has not named its web host or its content system. [1][2]

How attacks get in, and what is not known here

### The state has said nothing about the method. A widespread web flaw was fixed this month. No source connects the two.

- **The method.** Neither the office’s statement nor any report names how the attackers reached the Auditor of State’s web server, what software it runs, or whether it was patched. [1][2]
- **The state’s server, as archived.** The last archived copy of ohioauditor.gov before the attack, an Internet Archive capture of Oct. 17, 2026, is static HTML pages (default.html, financial.html, performance/default.html) with an ASP.NET audit search behind them (auditsearch/Search.aspx), jQuery 3.7.1 and Google Tag Manager. No PHP marker appears in the pages. On the record, then, the PHP flaw is a weak fit for the state’s web server, and a direct exposure for county sites built on PHP platforms, the Butler County Auditor’s Revize pages among them. The state has not named the method. [33][31]
- **The county’s pages.** The Butler County Auditor’s public pages run on Revize’s platform; the addresses end in .php, which is the mark of PHP, the language that builds the pages of about 69 in every 100 websites whose server language is known. [31][32]
- **PHP2Shell.** On October 21 the PHP project shipped fixes for two flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, that let anyone on the internet run commands on a site’s server with no login. Cloudflare’s chief executive posted that attempts on its network went from thousands before the fix to millions that night. The fix has to be installed on each server by whoever runs it. CISA said on October 21 it had not observed exploitation as of publication. [32]
- **What is on the record.** A flaw of this kind exists and is being tried at scale; many government sites run PHP; a county auditor’s site in Ohio is among them. Nothing on the record says whether Revize or any Ohio government has installed the fix, and nothing connects PHP2Shell to the attack on the state. [32][33]

**What a resident can ask, from the record.** Whether the office has an incident response plan under R.C. 9.64 and when it was last tested. What the Tyler, Revize and DocuPet contracts require on uptime, breach notice and data location. When the last independent security assessment was, and who did it. What the public will hear when a system goes down, how fast, and where. Each is a question about documents and dates; the law lets an office answer them without releasing the sealed records. [14]

**Related on the Well.** [PHP2Shell](https://tools.dnsc.ai/stories/php2shell/): what PHP is, how the attack works, who went offline, and what to ask your host. [Who owns the pipes](https://tools.dnsc.ai/civic/who-owns-the-pipes/): who owns the apps, networks and papers, and the local news in Butler County.

The editor’s take

Opinion. What follows is the editor’s view, apart from the reported record above.

The technology our society is built on is very vulnerable, and it always has been, because it has been under-resourced and run by people who don’t know what they’re doing. When we see our own state auditor’s office get attacked like this, with real vulnerabilities in our systems, get ready for a wave of attacks of this nature. We need leaders who are prepared to defend our country and our local communities in the new world of AI cyber attacks. What have municipalities and our leaders done to help prepare us and our systems to be secure? Every single thing on the record here is reactionary.

Dustin Nimmo, editor · Oct. 27, 2026

# Who owns the pipes

> Thirteen people and families hold the most votes behind the apps, networks and papers Americans use: who they are, everything they own, how many people each reaches, how a minority of the shares becomes control, and who owns local news across the country and in Butler County, Ohio, from the companies' own filings, October 2026.

## 13 people and families behind the apps, networks and papers.

Larry Page · Sergey Brin · Mark Zuckerberg · Elon Musk · Jeff Bezos · The Ellison family · Brian L. Roberts · The Murdoch family · Evan Spiegel · Robert Murphy · The Newhouse family · Donald J. Trump · The Ochs-Sulzberger family

YouTube reaches 84 percent of American adults and Facebook 71 percent, by Pew's count in 2025. Meta counts 3.6 billion people a day on its apps worldwide. The number of people and families who hold the most votes behind the apps, networks and papers here: 13. Nine people, four families. At Disney and at TikTok in the United States, no one is in control. [24] [36]

##### Larry Page and Sergey Brin

No. 3 and No. 4 in the world · $284 billion and $262 billion · Forbes Real Time, Oct. 14, 2026

Co-founders of Google. Both are Alphabet directors; Page chairs its executive committee. Neither runs the company: Sundar Pichai is chief executive of Google and Alphabet.

Together, 52.7 percent of Alphabet's votes (Page 27.4, Brin 25.3), through Class B shares that carry ten votes each.

Alphabet 2026 proxy [3] · Forbes [7]

A button: Close.

##### Mark Zuckerberg

No. 6 in the world · $252 billion · Forbes Real Time, Oct. 14, 2026

Founder, chairman and chief executive of Meta: Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger and Threads.

60.8 percent of Meta's votes. Meta calls itself a controlled company because of it.

Meta 2026 proxy [2] · Forbes [7]

A button: Close.

##### Elon Musk

No. 1 in the world · $941 billion · Forbes Real Time, Oct. 14, 2026

Founder, chief executive, chief technical officer and chairman of SpaceX, which owns X, xAI and Starlink. Chief executive of Tesla, where he holds about 20 percent.

About 82 percent of SpaceX's votes after its June 2026 offering.

SpaceX prospectus, June 12, 2026 [1] · Tesla 10-K · Forbes [7]

A button: Close.

##### Evan Spiegel and Robert Murphy

No. 1,761 and No. 2,358 in the world · $2.3 billion and $1.7 billion · Forbes Real Time, Oct. 14, 2026

Co-founders of Snap. Spiegel is chief executive; Murphy is chief technology officer. Both are directors.

Over 99 percent of Snap's votes between them; Spiegel alone holds a majority. Snap's publicly traded Class A shares carry no vote.

Snap 10-K and 10-Q, 2026 [35] · Forbes [7]

A button: Close.

##### Donald J. Trump

No. 598 in the world · $6.8 billion · Forbes Real Time, Oct. 14, 2026

President of the United States. His revocable trust holds 41 percent of Trump Media, which makes Truth Social. Donald J. Trump Jr., his son, is the trustee and votes the shares.

Trump Media has agreed to merge with TAE Technologies, a fusion energy company; the trust's share would become 22 percent.

Trump Media Form S-4, Sept. 30, 2026 [5] · Forbes [7]

A button: Close.

##### Advance, the Newhouse family

No live Forbes rank · about $24 billion for the family, Forbes as relayed by The New York Times, May 2026

Advance, founded by S.I. Newhouse in 1922, calls itself a private, family-held business. It owns Condé Nast and Advance Local, home of The Plain Dealer, and is among the largest holders of Reddit and Charter Communications.

Advance holds 65.2 percent of Reddit's votes. Reddit's chief executive, Steve Huffman, votes those shares under an irrevocable proxy. Steven Newhouse, a co-president of Advance, sits on Reddit's board; his cousin Michael Newhouse, also a co-president, on Charter's.

Reddit 2026 proxy [6] · Charter 2026 proxy · advance.com [39] · Forbes via NYT [7]

A button: Close.

##### TikTok in the United States: no one in control

Oracle 15% · Silver Lake 15% · MGX 15% · ByteDance 19.9%

**Oracle:** founded by Larry Ellison, who holds 38.2 percent.

**Silver Lake:** a private technology investment firm; its chief executive, Egon Durban, sits on the venture's board.

**MGX:** an Abu Dhabi AI investment company, chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan.

**ByteDance:** the company that built TikTok; it chooses one of seven directors.

TikTok, Jan. 23, 2026 [4] · Oracle proxy [23] · [45]

A button: Close.

##### The Ellison family

Larry Ellison: No. 8 in the world · $170 billion · Forbes Real Time, Oct. 14, 2026 · David Ellison: not public

**David Ellison** is chairman and chief executive of Skydance: CBS, CNN, HBO, Paramount and Warner Bros. As manager of the family's companies he controls Harbor Lights, which held all of Skydance's voting stock before the Oct. 6 close; since then the Ellison family and RedBird Capital are its only voting holders, by the closing release.

**Larry Ellison**, his father, founded Oracle in 1977 and is its executive chair and largest holder, 38.2 percent. He guaranteed $45.72 billion of the Warner Bros. Discovery purchase. Oracle holds 15 percent of TikTok's U.S. venture.

Skydance 10-K/A and 8-K [9] · Oracle proxy [23] · Forbes [7]

A button: Close.

##### Brian L. Roberts

No. 2,862 in the world · $1.3 billion · Forbes Real Time, Oct. 14, 2026

Chairman of Comcast since 2004 and its chief executive since 2002, now co-chief executive with Mike Cavanagh. Comcast owns NBC, Peacock, Telemundo, Bravo and Universal.

One third of the votes at Comcast and at Versant (MS NOW, CNBC), a share the filings call "generally non-dilutable," from Class B stock worth 0.3 percent of Comcast's shares.

Comcast and Versant 2026 proxies [11] · Forbes [7]

A button: Close.

##### Lachlan Murdoch and the Murdoch family

"Rupert Murdoch & family": No. 101 in the world · $24.8 billion · Forbes Real Time, Oct. 14, 2026

Lachlan Murdoch is executive chair and chief executive of Fox and chair of News Corp. Rupert Murdoch is chairman emeritus.

Trusts for Lachlan, Grace and Chloe Murdoch hold 38.8 percent of Fox's votes and 34.8 percent of News Corp's. The 2025 settlement put the vote with a managing director Lachlan appoints; the 2026 proxy says he does not control LGC Holdco.

Fox and News Corp 2026 proxies [12][16] · Forbes [7]

A button: Close.

##### Disney: no one in control

Vanguard 8.5% · BlackRock 6.9% · one vote a share

The Walt Disney Company owns ABC and ABC News, ESPN, Hulu and Disney+. Josh D'Amaro has been chief executive since March 18, 2026. No holder has more than 8.5 percent of the vote.

**Vanguard** runs index funds, which hold the stocks in a market index such as the S&P 500. Vanguard is owned by its funds, and the funds by their more than 50 million investors. Its stewardship team casts the funds' votes; in 32 funds, investors can pick a voting policy themselves.

Disney 2026 proxy and 8-Ks [13] · Vanguard [46]

A button: Close.

##### Jeff Bezos

No. 2 in the world · $373 billion · Forbes Real Time, Oct. 14, 2026

Founder and executive chair of Amazon, where he holds 8.8 percent. He owns The Washington Post through Nash Holdings, an entity that belongs to Mr. Bezos in his individual capacity, bought in 2013 for $250 million, and Blue Origin. Amazon owns AWS, Prime Video, Amazon MGM Studios and Whole Foods Market.

Amazon 2026 proxy · Washington Post Co. 8-K, 2013 [15] · Forbes [7]

A button: Close.

##### The Ochs-Sulzberger family trust

Net worth not public

Created in 1997 to maintain the editorial independence and the integrity of The New York Times. It holds 94.6 percent of the Class B shares, which elect 9 of the 13 directors. A. G. Sulzberger, chairman and publisher, is one of its eight trustees.

New York Times Co. 2026 proxy [17]

The holders

### Who they are, and what they hold.

**Each holder: the companies, the stakes, the net worth, their own words**

The platforms

### At SpaceX, Meta and Alphabet, the founders hold the vote.

Their shares carry ten votes each. SpaceX and Meta each describe themselves in their filings as a controlled company. [1][2][3]

[Image: Elon Musk at the Pentagon.]

Pentagon, March 21, 2025 · DoD photo, public domain

#### SpaceX, which owns X and xAI Elon Musk

**82** percent of the SpaceX vote, approximately, after the June 2026 offering [1]

SpaceX's prospectus calls X our real-time information, entertainment, and free speech platform that serves as a foundational distribution and data engine for the AI ecosystem. [1]

**What he holds**About 82 percent of SpaceX's voting power and 91.6 percent of its Class B stock, which elects 51 percent of the board, per the final prospectus of June 12, 2026. SpaceX market value about $2.0 trillion, Oct. 14. Net worth $949.8 billion, Forbes, Oct. 14. [1][7][8]

**What he gives**About $366 million to federal political committees in the 2025 to 2026 election cycle, by his own team's count to The New York Times, Oct. 12, confirmed by his super PAC's spokesman. The federal filings are due Oct. 15. In 2024: more than $290 million, per federal filings reported by CNN. [21][22]

**X, by the numbers**

The prospectus: over 1.3 billion accounts active in the last twelve months ended March 2026, including approximately 550 million monthly active AI users across Grok and X. It warns the count may include fake and automated accounts. [1]

On August 14, 2026 SpaceX issued 389,289,254 new shares to buy Cursor. No filing since restates Musk's percentage; the June figure stands. [1]

[Image: Mark Zuckerberg, studio portrait.]

September 2025 · Jeff Sainlar for Meta, CC BY-SA 4.0

#### Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Threads Mark Zuckerberg

**60.8** percent of the Meta vote, April 1, 2026 [2]

Because Mr. Zuckerberg controls a majority of our outstanding voting power, we are a ‘controlled company’

**Meta Platforms** · 2026 proxy statement, April 16 [2]

**What he holds**341,823,978 Class B shares, 99.8 percent of that class, at ten votes each. Meta market value about $1.87 trillion, Oct. 14. Net worth $252.3 billion, Forbes, Oct. 14. [2][7][8]

[Image: Larry Page.][Image: Sergey Brin.]

Page, TED 2014 · Steve Jurvetson, CC BY 2.0. Brin, 2016 · State Department, public domain

#### Google, YouTube Larry Page and Sergey Brin

**52.7** percent of the Alphabet vote between them: Page 27.4, Brin 25.3, April 6, 2026 [3]

Neither runs the company. Sundar Pichai is chief executive of Google and Alphabet; Neal Mohan is chief executive of YouTube. Alphabet's Class C shares, about 5.5 billion of them, have no voting power. [3]

**What they hold**Page: 389,051,160 Class B shares. Brin: 358,939,978 Class B shares. Alphabet market value about $4.2 trillion, Oct. 14. Net worth: Page $287.1 billion, Brin $264.2 billion, Forbes, Oct. 14. [3][7][8]

**Reddit:** Advance, the Newhouse family's company, held 65.2 percent of Reddit's vote on March 31, 2026; Steve Huffman votes Advance's shares by irrevocable proxy. Advance also owns The Plain Dealer in Cleveland. [6][20]

**Truth Social: Donald J. Trump's trust holds 41 percent of Trump Media**

[Image: Donald J. Trump, official portrait.]

Official portrait, 2025 · Daniel Torok, White House, public domain

#### Truth Social · Trump Media & Technology Group Donald J. Trump

**41** percent of Trump Media, held by his revocable trust, Sept. 15, 2026 [5]

The trust's sole trustee is Donald J. Trump Jr.; the President is its settlor and sole beneficiary. Trump Media has agreed to merge with TAE Technologies, a fusion energy company; if it closes, the trust's share becomes 22 percent of the combined company. [5]

**What the trust holds**114,750,000 shares, per the Form S-4 filed Sept. 30, 2026. Trump Media market value about $2.0 billion, Oct. 14. Net worth $6.8 billion, Forbes, Oct. 14. [5][7][8]

**Who is Vanguard?** A fund company. Its index funds hold the stocks in a market index, such as the S&P 500, for the people who invest in them: more than 50 million, nearly 5 million of them through workplace retirement plans Vanguard runs. Vanguard is owned by its funds, and the funds by those investors. A Vanguard stewardship team casts the funds' votes at Disney and every other company they hold; in 32 index funds, investors can choose a voting policy of their own.

How control works

### Some shares carry ten or fifteen votes. Some carry none.

Black: the holder's share of the company's stock. Red: the holder's share of the vote.

**Alphabet** Larry Page and Sergey Brin

[Chart: Alphabet: Larry Page and Sergey Brin owns 6.2% of the shares and holds 52.7% of the vote]

Class B carries ten votes; Class C carries none. [3]

**Comcast** Brian L. Roberts

[Chart: Comcast: Brian L. Roberts owns 0.3% of the shares and holds 33.3% of the vote]

Class B carries fifteen votes a share. [11]

**Snap** Evan Spiegel and Robert Murphy

[Chart: Snap: Evan Spiegel and Robert Murphy owns 13.5% of the shares and holds 99%+ of the vote]

Class C, ten votes a share, is 13.5% of all shares; Class A has no vote. [35]

**The New York Times** Ochs-Sulzberger Trust

[Chart: The New York Times: Ochs-Sulzberger Trust owns 1.3% of the shares and holds 9 of 13 of the vote]

Class B elects nine of thirteen directors. [17]

**SpaceX, Skydance, Fox, News Corp and Trump Media**

**SpaceX:** Elon Musk holds about 82 percent of the vote and 91.6 percent of the Class B stock, which elects 51 percent of the board, per the June 2026 prospectus. The prospectus states no single figure for his share of all stock. [1]

**Skydance:** only Class A stock votes, and Harbor Lights, about 77.5 percent owned by Ellison family entities, held all of it. [9]

**Fox and News Corp:** only Class B stock votes. LGC Holdco, owned equally by trusts for Lachlan, Grace and Chloe Murdoch, holds 38.8 percent of Fox's Class B and 34.8 percent of News Corp's. [12][16]

**Trump Media:** one class of stock, one vote a share. The President's trust holds 41 percent of both. [5]

Shares of stock: arithmetic from each proxy's share counts. Meta: 342.5 million of 2,538.4 million shares. Alphabet: 748.0 million of 12,115.8 million, counting Class C. Comcast: 9.4 million of 3,573.8 million. The New York Times: 2.1 million of 161.9 million. [2][3][11][17]

TikTok in the United States

### Oracle, Silver Lake and MGX hold 15 percent each. ByteDance holds 19.9.

Since January 2026 a joint venture runs TikTok in the United States. No one holds a majority. [4]

[Chart: TikTok USDS Joint Venture: Oracle 15 percent, Silver Lake 15, MGX 15, together 45; ByteDance 19.9; other investors 35.1 by subtraction]

Oracle, Silver Lake and MGX together: 45 percent, short of a majority. With ByteDance, the four named holders: 64.9 percent. [4]

1. **15%** **Larry Ellison** Founded Oracle in 1977; holds 38.2 percent and is executive chair.
2. **15%** **Egon Durban** Silver Lake’s chief executive; sits on the venture’s seven-member board.
3. **MGX** **15%** **Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan** Chairs MGX; Abu Dhabi’s deputy ruler and the UAE’s national security adviser.
4. **19.9%** ZY **Zhang Yiming** Co-founded ByteDance in 2012; No. 24 in the world, $84 billion, by Forbes. AD **Arthur Dantchik** Susquehanna; an investor on ByteDance’s board. **William Ford** General Atlantic; an investor on ByteDance’s board. PL **Philippe Laffont** Coatue; an investor on ByteDance’s board. State **The Chinese state** 1 percent of Beijing ByteDance Technology, a ByteDance subsidiary in China; names one of its directors.
5. **+8** **35.1%** other investors **Eight other investors**, Dell Family Office and seven more. The venture publishes no percentages for them.

**Each owner, in full**

**Oracle, 15%.** The company Larry Ellison founded in 1977. He holds 38.2 percent and is executive chair; his son David runs Skydance. TikTok's U.S. algorithm is to be secured in Oracle's U.S. cloud environment. [4] [23]

**Silver Lake, 15%.** A private investment firm that buys into technology companies, about $126 billion under management. Its chief executive, Egon Durban, sits on the venture's seven-member board. [4] [39]

**MGX, 15%.** Abu Dhabi's AI investment company, set up in March 2024 by an AI council the UAE's president created, with Mubadala and G42 as founding partners. Its chairman, Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, is Abu Dhabi's deputy ruler and the UAE's national security adviser. [45] [39]

**ByteDance, 19.9%.** The company that built TikTok, founded in 2012 by Zhang Yiming and Liang Rubo. By TikTok's count in 2024, global investors own about 60 percent of ByteDance, its co-founders 20 and its employees 20. Investors on its board include Arthur Dantchik of Susquehanna, William Ford of General Atlantic and Philippe Laffont of Coatue. Zhang Yiming is No. 24 in the world, $84 billion, by Forbes. ByteDance chooses one of the venture's seven directors. [4] [7] [45]

**The Chinese state.** Since April 2021, a company owned by three Chinese state entities holds 1 percent of Beijing ByteDance Technology, a ByteDance subsidiary in China, and the government names one of its directors, as reported by Reuters in August 2021. [45]

**Eight other investors, 35.1%** by subtraction: Dell Family Office, Vastmere Strategic Investments, Alpha Wave Partners, Revolution, Merritt Way, Via Nova, Virgo LI and NJJ Capital. The venture publishes no percentages for them. [4]

**The board and the ads**

A seven-member board; ByteDance chooses one. The White House required ByteDance to hold less than 20% of the stock as required by law. Advertising stays with TikTok global's U.S. entities, outside the venture. [4]

Among American adults who use TikTok, 55 percent regularly get news there, Pew, 2025. [26]

Local news, across the country

### Where six companies own local TV stations.

Each dot is a television market where the company owns or runs a station, from its own station table. Cincinnati is circled.

Television and radio brands in nine markets, by its own brands page. Apollo funds bought a majority of it in 2019 and Cox Enterprises kept a minority stake, by Cox's release. In Dayton, WHIO.

**868** radio stations in about 160 markets, iHeartMedia, including 700 WLW and 55KRC. No one in control; largest holder PIMCO, 17.4 percent.

In Butler County

### The local paper, the stations and the radio, and who owns each.

Butler County has one daily newspaper. Medill's 2025 count of local news outlets lists one newspaper and one digital news site in the county. [29][33]

**Journal-News** *one family* Cox First Media, part of Cox Enterprises, a family-owned enterprise. Prints Sunday through Friday. [29]

**The Cincinnati Enquirer** no controller · USA TODAY Co., formerly Gannett. Largest holder 9.7%. [19]

**WKRC Local 12 (CBS)** *one family* Sinclair. The four Smith brothers hold 80.6% of the vote. [14]

**WCPO 9 (ABC)** *one family* E.W. Scripps. The Scripps family agreement holds 93.3% of the voting shares. [14]

**WLWT (NBC)** Hearst · Hearst Television. [20]

**WXIX FOX19** *one family* Gray Media. Hilton Howell Jr., his wife and Harriett Robinson hold over 48.5% of the vote. [14]

**700 WLW, 55KRC** no controller iHeartMedia. Largest holder of the voting stock, PIMCO, 17.4%. [32]

**WVXU 91.7, WMUB 88.5** nonprofit · Cincinnati Public Radio, a 501(c)(3). [31]

**Oxford Free Press** nonprofit · An independent nonprofit newspaper with 501(c)(3) status founded in June 2024. Weekly, 1,900 copies. [30][31]

**What closed, merged or stopped printing**

1. Nov. 2013 · The Middletown Journal is merged into the Journal-News, making Butler a one-newspaper county, in the paper's own words. [29]
2. Mar. 5, 2022 · The Enquirer stops printing on Saturdays. [30]
3. May 6, 2023 · The Journal-News stops printing on Saturdays. [30]
4. Jan. 2024 · Cox closes the Oxford Press, published since 1936. The Oxford Free Press opens as a nonprofit that year. [30]
5. Mar. 2026 · The Cincinnati Herald, the city's Black weekly since 1955, pauses operations, as reported by WKRC. [34]

Nationally, Northwestern's Medill school counts 212 counties with no local news source and about 3,500 newspapers gone since 2005, in its 2025 report. By Medill's count, Butler County has one newspaper and one digital news site. [33]

An undated Report for America profile says the Enquirer once had a seven-person bureau for Butler, Warren and Clermont counties, then went a year with no reporter there. [30]

Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance but for our entire industry.

**David Ellison**, chairman and chief executive · Oct. 6, 2026 [9]

**How the deal went**

December 5, 2025: Netflix agreed to buy Warner Bros., HBO and HBO Max, after a spin-off of CNN and the cable channels. February 27, 2026: Warner Bros. Discovery ended the Netflix deal and took Paramount's offer of $31 a share in cash; Paramount paid Netflix's $2.8 billion termination fee. Shareholders approved on April 23. [9]

Twelve states sued and settled on September 21. As reported by Reuters, the terms include independent editorial boards for CBS and CNN. A federal judge approved the decree on September 30. Mark Thompson stays as CNN's editor in chief and Bari Weiss as CBS News's, per Al Jazeera, Oct. 6. [10]

# HomeView

> On October 13, 2026 Apple announced HomeView, a $299 home hub with a screen, a camera and Siri AI: what it does, how a home connects to it, what stays in the house and what leaves it, and a day with it.

DNSC · From the public record

HomeView · October 16, 2026 · Understanding the week, from the record

Apple · Oct. 13, 2026

## HomeView, Apple's $299 kitchen hub, recognizes six faces and runs the lights and locks

HomeView is Apple's new small AI computer for the kitchen counter: a 7-inch screen on a speaker, with a camera and Apple's A18 chip. It runs Siri AI, recognizes up to six people by face and controls a home's lights, locks, cameras and thermostat. Apple announced it on October 13; it costs $299 and arrives November 13. [1][2]

Published October 16, 2026

[Image: Two Apple HomeView hubs on their round speaker bases. One screen shows home controls: the living room thermostat at 68, a front door lock, entryway lights and a good morning scene. The other screen plays music.]

Photo: Apple

**$299** U.S. price

**Nov. 13** in stores

6

HomeView

### Central to the home and personal to everyone in it. [1]

#### Six faces

HomeView recognizes up to six people and delivers a personalized experience for each one. [1]

#### Each person's own

Messages and Calendar appear only when the enrolled user is recognized by their face, and when their paired iPhone or iPad is present. [1]

[Interactive: A drawn HomeView on its speaker base. Its screen changes between the household screen, the screen of one recognized person, and a guest's screen., drawn by the page in your browser.]

#### Shared by all

Shared photo albums and music can be easily enjoyed by everyone in a household, including guests. [1]

#### Siri AI

Anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer. [1]

hub

The hub

### Lights, locks, cameras and the thermostat connect to HomeView.

**In Apple's words**

**The hub:** Apple HomeView is a central hub for your smart home accessories. [2] A hub lets a household control your smart home accessories while you're away from home, share control of your accessories with others, and automate your accessories to do what you want, when you want. [10]

**Lights, locks, cameras, thermostat:** HomeView lets users control the home by touch or with just their voice using Siri AI: viewing camera feeds, adjusting the thermostat and lights, locking doors, or closing the blinds. The Home Camera face can livestream up to nine video feeds at once. [1]

**iPhone:** When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled device, it can also draw on a user's personal context, such as their Calendar, Messages, and relevant information across their apps. [1]

**Apple's cloud:** Siri requests on HomeView can use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy of the device to the cloud. [1]

Also hubs, in the same lineup

**Apple TV 4K** It continues to serve as a powerful home hub. $299, Nov. 13. [4]

**HomePod mini 2** HomePod mini acts as a home hub. $149, Oct. 30; Siri AI in a future software update. [3][9]

A18

Privacy

### What stays in the house and what leaves it.

#### In the house

- **Secure Exclaves**Camera and microphone feeds, in a compartment that cannot be accessed by the operating system or by Apple. [2]
- **On device**Simple requests in the Home app: your data never leaves your device. [8]
- **Camera recordings** Analyzed privately on your Apple devices at home. [8]

#### Leaves the house

- **Private Cloud Compute**Used for complex requests. Data there is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else. [1][8]
- **Camera recordings** Sent securely to iCloud through end-to-end encryption. [8]
- **Siri requests** Associated with a random identifier, not your Apple Account. [8]

**The models, on both sides:** custom-built in collaboration with Google and its Gemini models, they run on device and on servers using Private Cloud Compute. [6]

**More from the record**

#### The hub line

Apple names four home hubs: HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K. [7] When you set up HomePod mini and HomePod, they automatically become home hubs. [10] iPad isn't supported as a home hub on the latest version of Apple Home. [11]

Chips: HomeView A18, Apple TV 4K A19, HomePod mini 2 S10. [2][3][4] HomePod mini can recognize up to six users in a household by their voice. [3] Apple TV 4K supports secure local processing of HomeKit Secure Video. [4]

Mac mini with M6 is on none of Apple's hub lists. [7][10][11] Of it, Apple says: Create your own AI agents for anything from running a household to running a business. Mac mini enables fast, private, on-device inference. [12] The new HomePod mini can serve as a speaker for Mac. [3]

#### The device

A 7-inch Liquid Retina screen (6.98 inches measured diagonally), 500 nits down to 0.3; the A18 chip; a 12MP Center Stage camera; four beamforming microphones; on a speaker base or wall-mounted. FaceTime, Intercom, recipes as steps with timers, and an alert to each person's iPhone, iPad or Apple Watch when it hears a smoke or carbon monoxide alarm. Setup and multiple users require a compatible iPhone or iPad. [1][2]

#### Security, further

Home data is stored in a way that Apple can't read it. [7] Home Collection camera footage, for users with iCloud+, is stored encrypted in iCloud for 10 days. [5]

Apple's five requirements for Private Cloud Compute, 2024: stateless computation, enforceable guarantees, no privileged runtime access, non-targetability, verifiable transparency. User devices will be willing to send data only to PCC nodes that can cryptographically attest to running publicly listed software. [14] Outside experts can continue to verify this privacy promise at any time. [6]

#### The models and the servers

The next generation of Apple Foundation Models will be based on Google's Gemini models and cloud technology. Google and Apple, Jan. 12, 2026. [15] In addition to its own data center infrastructure, the Company relies on third-party cloud service providers to meet these compute needs. Apple 10-Q, July 31, 2026. [16] Features on server-side models are subject to daily usage limits. Expanded access to such features will be available for a fee in the future. [1]

#### Who can use it

Guests can still easily interact with HomeView to control smart home accessories, check the weather, set timers, and play music, without accessing anyone's personal information. [2] Siri AI is not available for users under 13. [6] Without an Apple Intelligence iPhone or iPad, HomeView still brings Siri AI's broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery. [1]

#### More of the day

At the door, a chime sounds through HomeView, HomePod, or HomePod mini. [5] In the kitchen, recipes become step-by-step instructions with hands-free timer control. [1] Keep an eye on the game while you do the dishes. [2] At night, locks and motion sensors that activate when it's bedtime. [21]

#### Prices and dates

HomeView $299, pre-orders from Oct. 13; it arrives Nov. 13 in Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, the UK and the U.S., and in Singapore and South Africa; Siri AI on it is a beta, in English. Apple HomeView is not available for sale in the European Union, as Siri AI is currently unavailable in iOS in the EU. Wall mounts from Schneider Home $59.95, $79.95, and $129.95 in early 2027. [1] Apple TV 4K $299, Nov. 13; HomePod mini 2 $149, Oct. 30; HomePod $349; Mac mini with M6 from $899, in stores since Sept. 22. [3][4][13][20] Apple Home Collection (cameras, a doorbell, a lock, thermostats): December, some in early 2027; cameras from $199.95, the lock $349.95, thermostats $199.95. [5] iCloud+ for home cameras: $0.99 a month records one camera, $2.99 up to five, $9.99 and up any number. [19]

#### The count

Apple's active devices on Jan. 29, 2026: more than 2.5 billion. On July 30 the count reached a new all-time high. [17][18] Services sales in the quarter ended June 27, 2026: $30.7 billion, about 28 percent of Apple's $109.4 billion. [16]

0.3

A day with it

### Morning, leaving, coming home, bedtime.

1. #### Morning One “Good Morning” scene can simultaneously adjust the thermostat, tilt an indoor camera down while a user is getting ready, and start music on HomePod. [5]
2. #### Leaving As the last user leaves for work, the thermostat adjusts for an empty home, the door locks, and cameras begin monitoring again. [5]
3. #### Coming home The front door unlocks automatically as they approach. [5]
4. #### Bedtime The screen dims down to just 0.3 nits, making it ideal for the nightstand. [1]

# PHP2Shell

> On October 21, 2026 PHP shipped fixes for two flaws, nicknamed PHP2Shell, that let anyone on the internet run commands on a website’s server without logging in. Cloudflare’s CEO posted that its network saw millions of attempts by that night. What PHP is, how the attack works, who went offline, what to ask your host, the 34 hours from leak to millions of attempts, and who found it with AI.

DNSC · From the public record

PHP2Shell · October 22, 2026 · Understanding the week, from the record

PHP · Cloudflare · Oct. 20 to 22, 2026

## PHP fixed two flaws that let anyone on the internet run commands on a website’s server. Cloudflare saw millions of attempts within 12 hours of the fix.

PHP is the programming language that builds the pages of about 69 in every 100 websites whose server language is known. [23] On October 21 the PHP project shipped fixes for two flaws, nicknamed PHP2Shell, that let anyone run their own commands on a site’s server over the web, with no login. [1][6] That night Cloudflare’s chief executive posted that attempts to use them on its network had gone from thousands, in the 10 hours before the announcement, to millions. [13]

[Chart: 100 squares stand for 100 websites whose server-side language W3Techs can identify. 69 are filled: the ones running PHP.]

69 of 100

websites whose server-side language is known run PHP, by W3Techs’ count on Oct. 22, 2026. [23]

PHP’s own site: it powers everything from your blog to the most popular websites in the world. [11]

The fix has to be installed on each server by whoever runs it; updating the website itself does not fix PHP. [6][12] On October 21 BambooHR’s HR and payroll service and Dutch government sites went offline as a precaution. [19][20]

Not yet published

**Disclosure:** Anthropic is the company that makes Claude, the AI that helps make this site. The PHP Foundation says it worked with Alpha-Omega to scan PHP with Anthropic’s Claude Mythos earlier this year, and thanks Alpha-Omega, OpenAI and Anthropic for giving the team access to their tools and funding some of the security work. Anthropic is not among the finders it credits for these two flaws. [5]

What it is

### A web request can trigger the attack before the site’s own code runs.

- **PHP the language**: A programming language that runs on a website’s server and builds each page before it reaches a visitor’s browser. WordPress, Drupal, Nextcloud and phpMyAdmin are built on it. [22]
- **Shell the command line**: A computer’s command line. Having a shell on a server means being able to type commands on it from far away. PHP2Shell is the name the finders gave the pair. [6]
- **Remote code execution RCE**: Running commands on someone else’s computer over the internet. Unauthenticated means no login first. PHP rates both flaws 9.2 out of 10. [2][3][4]
- **WAF web application firewall**: A filter in front of a site that checks each request and blocks ones that match known attacks. Cloudflare turned on rules for these flaws for its customers, free plans included. [12]

Drawn from PHP’s advisory and the two GitHub advisories [1][3][4]; the leaked items are the ones Wiz lists. [7]

**The two flaws, in PHP’s words**

**CVE-2026-109618, RCE via OOM corruption:** out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid. [1] The confirmed impact is unauthenticated remote code execution as the web worker account. [3]

**CVE-2026-109619, RCE via stale global state:** request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it. [1] Session upload progress can reach session handling before ordinary session initialization. Its confirmed impact includes memory disclosure and remote code execution. [4]

**Who is at risk:** all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs. [1] For PHP-FPM, the advisory says no complete exploit has been shown. [3]

**What can leak:** Wiz says leaked memory may hold passwords, authentication tokens, API keys and certificates from other requests or the server. [7]

The race

### Thousands of attempts before the fix, millions by that night.

> In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the @Cloudflare network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it. That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now. [13] · Matthew Prince, Cloudflare’s chief executive, on X, 9:25 PM ET Wednesday, Oct. 21 (01:25 UTC Thursday)

Attempts on Cloudflare’s network, log scale: each step up is ten times more. Each bar spans the range of Prince’s word (thousands is 1,000 to 9,999); his post gives no exact counts. Times are Eastern. [12][13]

- **Attempts.** CISA said on Oct. 21 that it has not observed exploitation of these vulnerabilities as of the time of publication. [18] The Dutch National Cyber Security Centre said a day later, We see attempts to exploit the vulnerabilities. (translated) [21] No source on the record confirms a successful break-in. [27]
- **Before the fix.** Cloudflare says it turned its rules on at 3:02 a.m. UTC on Oct. 21, for all plans with its firewall, free included. That was nearly 11 hours before PHP’s 14:00 UTC release. [1][12] Its chief technology officer posted that morning that PHP sites behind Cloudflare already have an initial set of WAF rules deployed. [14]
- **Changing payloads.** Cloudflare says attackers changed their payloads to try to get past the rules. [12]
- **Four days earlier.** Amazon says its honeypots caught one attempt dated Oct. 17, and that it remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure. It adds, it’s unclear if any of these attempts would have succeeded in real-world systems. [17]

Who it reaches

### Where PHP runs, and who went offline to patch it.

40of 100

of all websites run WordPress (39.6, by W3Techs’ count), which is built on PHP. [22][24] Wiz says it confirmed the attack against WordPress and Drupal in August. [7]

[Chart: 100 squares for all websites; 39.6 filled: WordPress.]

20of 100

of all websites send their traffic through Cloudflare, by Cloudflare’s count; W3Techs measures 27.8. [15][25]

[Chart: 100 squares for all websites; 20 filled: Cloudflare, by its own count.]

35of 100

PHP sites run version 7 or 5 (26.9 and 7.7), lines that no longer get releases from the PHP project. [1][23]

[Chart: 100 squares for PHP websites; 34.6 filled: version 7 or 5.]

#### Taken offline as a precaution, Oct. 21

As each one announced it, or as reported.

- **BambooHR**HR and payroll, in the U.S., Canada and Ireland: We know this interrupts essential work, including payroll. [19] midnight ET · 7:51 AM to 2:01 PM midnight
- **The Netherlands**MijnOverheid and DigiD (the government’s online services and log-in), the House of Representatives’ site, the National Cyber Security Centre’s own site, the Data Protection Authority, Notubiz (a meeting system used by about 100 municipalities) and several university systems. [20]
- **Finland and Japan**Finland’s state IT provider, Valtori, shut government public web services and said the outages were not caused by exploitation of the vulnerabilities or by a cyber breach. Japan’s National Tax Agency took its service down; the Finance Ministry and Meteorological Agency partly suspended theirs. [29]
- **University of Washington**Cut network access to systems running vulnerable PHP until each was patched, leaving them running. [22]

What to do

### Update PHP on the server, or ask your host whether it has.

PHP: There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice. [1]

**Fixed versions [1][18]**

| If you run | Fixed in | Note |
|---|---|---|
| PHP 8.5 | 8.5.12 |  |
| PHP 8.4 | 8.4.27 |  |
| PHP 8.3 | 8.3.36 |  |
| PHP 8.2 | 8.2.35 | End of life Dec. 31, 2026 |
| 7.4 to 8.1 | no release | PHP posted source patches; some vendors ship fixes |
| 5.4 to 7.3 | no fix | PHP: upgrade to a supported version |

CISA: systems that can’t be updated right away, or that run PHP 8.1 or earlier, should go offline until they can be patched or updated. [18]

**If you can’t update today: PHP’s stopgaps**

PHP says these reduce exposure to specific attack paths but do not make an installation safe. [1]

**For CVE-2026-109618:** set `memory_limit=-1` where applications can’t override it; set a low `post_max_size` (8M without uploads, 32M with); enforce request-size limits at the web server or proxy; do not use `RLIMIT_AS` or `RLIMIT_DATA`. [1]

**For CVE-2026-109619:** Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and restart every worker. On PHP 8.5, also set `fatal_error_backtraces=0` and restart every worker. [1]

**Signs to look for:** unexpectedly large or malformed PHPSESSID response cookies, unusual multipart requests (uploads) followed by memory-limit errors or repeated HTTP 500 responses, unexplained PHP worker crashes or restarts [6], and PHP worker processes launching shells or downloading tools. [18] The finders say the absence of these signs does not establish that a system is unaffected. [6]

#### If a host or vendor runs PHP for you

1. Cloudflare’s advice: ask your hosting provider to apply the fix if it manages PHP. Updating the site’s code or plugins alone does not fix these flaws. [12]
2. PHP: Linux distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance, so check your vendor for updated packages. [1]
3. A vendor’s fix can carry an older-looking version number. Debian advises looking for the CVE number in the package changelog. [27] Debian’s fixed builds are 8.2.35-1~deb12u1 and 8.4.27-1~deb13u1. [26]

#### If you run it yourself

1. Update to a fixed version, then restart Apache, PHP-FPM and any long-running PHP workers. Updating only the application does not fix the PHP runtime. [6]
2. CISA: find every system running PHP, including PHP built into other software; patch the internet-facing ones first; take systems offline if they can’t be updated right away; a web application firewall may offer partial protection until then. [18] The UK’s cyber agency also says to consider taking a system offline until it is fixed. [31]
3. CERT-EU: Only an update fully fixes these vulnerabilities. [30]

The 34 hours

### From leaked ID numbers to millions of attempts, Tuesday to Wednesday night.

Times are Eastern (EDT). UTC is four hours later. The release was set for Thursday; PHP moved it up a day after the leak. [2][5][28]

leak and fix defenders attempts seen taken offline hollow: a notice or a none seen · Sources: [1][2][5][12][13][16][19][20][27][28]

**Each time, and where it comes from**

**Tue. ~11 AM ET (15:00 UTC):** the two CVE IDs began circulating on online forums and social media. [5] A now-deleted Hacker News post said the flaws would be disclosed on October 22, as BleepingComputer reported. [28]

**Tue. 3:30 PM ET (19:30 UTC):** the Foundation says PHP brought its pre-announcement forward and published it at 19:30 UTC. [5] The notice set the release for Wednesday, 21 October 2026 at 14:00 UTC and said, We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public. [2] BleepingComputer reported it at 4:56 PM ET. [28] The Foundation says it moved the release from October 22nd, 14:00 UTC, to October 21st, 14:00 UTC. [5]

**Tue. ~4 PM ET (around 20:00 UTC):** as a result of the leak and pre-announcement, Calif mistakenly published a video of its exploits working, per the PHP Foundation. [5]

**Tue. 11:02 PM ET (03:02 UTC Wed.):** Cloudflare’s rules on by default. [12]

**Wed. 3:41 AM ET (07:41 UTC):** more than six hours before the coordinated release, Chainguard published built images with the fix; the Foundation says it unilaterally broke the embargo. [5]

**Wed. by 5:10 AM ET:** NOS, at 11:10 Amsterdam time, lists Dutch government and education sites taken offline as a precaution. [20]

**Wed. 7:26 AM and 10:19 AM ET (11:26 and 14:19 UTC):** watchTowr reported no exploitation, then attempts in its honeypots, as The Hacker News logged; watchTowr’s own page went up at 14:19 UTC. [16][27]

**Wed. 7:51 AM to 2:01 PM ET (11:51 to 18:01 UTC):** BambooHR offline, then back online following security patching and validation. [19]

**Wed. 10 AM ET (14:00 UTC):** PHP releases 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. [1] The Foundation says its team did not identify any functional exploits at the time of release/public disclosure. [5]

**Wed. 9:25 PM ET (01:25 UTC Thu.):** Prince’s post. Reuters calls it late Wednesday; outlets on UTC date it Thursday. [13][29]

How long it lived

### The affected releases go back to PHP 5.4, from March 2012.

Years run left to right; the dashed box on the axis is the zoomed stretch. [5][7][8][9][10]

- **2004.** Stefan Esser’s advisory: an attacker could trigger the memory_limit request termination in places where an interruption is unsafe and run code on PHP servers. [9] Calif traces its find to that line of research. [8]
- **2012.** PHP 5.4.0 came out March 1, 2012. [10] Wiz says releases back to PHP 5.4 are affected. [7]
- **2024.** While fixing one of the issues Quarkslab reported, a PHP core developer contracted by the PHP Foundation found the first signs of the OOM problem behind CVE-2026-109618. Then, a potential exploit for the OOM problem was theorized, but no concrete vectors were found. [5]
- **The delay.** We won’t pretend otherwise: the delay was a structural failure, caused by both the security team’s decision process and its lack of resources. The Foundation says it has since added people, a security team and tools. [5]
- **71 days** from Calif’s first report on Aug. 11 to the fix on Oct. 21. [5][8]

Who found it

### Three research teams, working with AI models, found it and reported it.

#### Calif

Ryan Austin

Found Aug. 1 · reported Aug. 11

Joined OpenAI’s Patch the Planet program July 30, where PHP stood out as a high-impact target. [8]

> Models do not reliably begin with obscure twenty-year-old exploitation primitives. [8]

#### OpenAI Codex Security

Amy Burnett

Same root cause · more on Sept. 18

OpenAI independently reported the same root cause as Calif, followed by further attack vectors from OpenAI on September 18th, the PHP Foundation says. [5]

#### Wiz Research

Sagi Tzadik, Shir Tamari, Nir Ohfeld, Tomer Schwartz

Found Aug. 19 · reported Aug. 24

Used Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol, by Wiz’s account. [7]

> a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work. [7]

#### The PHP security team

Confirmed Calif’s proof of concept Aug. 15 [8] and acknowledged Wiz’s reports Sept. 21. [7] The three teams worked with the PHP security team and the Gemini team at Google on discovery, coordination and patch verification. [6]

#### Oct. 21: the fix

8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. [1]

> No model is simply capable of unearthing all bugs with simple prompts. At least for now. [8] · Calif

> AI helps the team validate reports and group reports sharing the same root cause, and a person makes every call and works on every patch. [5] · The PHP Foundation

> Frontier models helped work through complex exploit chains and adapt them across different deployments. [6] · The three research teams, on php2shell.com

# Two pledges

> On October 18, 2026 Anthropic committed 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund, subject to a stockholder vote. On October 19 Elon Musk posted that next year he will give one SpaceX share to every kid in America. What each pledge commits, who decides, what has to happen first, and what is not yet known.

DNSC · From the public record

Two pledges · October 21, 2026 · Understanding the week, from the record

Anthropic · Elon Musk · Oct. 18 and 19, 2026

## Anthropic pledges 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund. Elon Musk pledges one SpaceX share to every kid in America.

Anthropic, the AI company, said on October 18 that 5% of its shares will go into a new fund that could give to nonprofits or make direct distributions to groups of people, once its stockholders approve. [1] The next day Elon Musk, who runs SpaceX, posted that next year he will give one of his SpaceX shares to every kid in America. [3][4]

If both go through, a child's account could hold a share of SpaceX, and a fund owned by an AI company could give to charities or straight to groups of people. Neither pledge has a date for the first share to move. [1][5][6][8]

Not yet published

**Disclosure:** Anthropic is the company that makes Claude, the AI that helps make this site.

### Anthropic

[Chart: 100 squares stand for all of Anthropic's shares. 5 are filled: the Fund, subject to a stockholder vote.]

5 of 100

of all Anthropic's shares, to the Fund, if stockholders approve. [1]

the Fund

### Elon Musk

[Chart: 100 squares stand for the roughly 4.8 billion SpaceX shares Musk owns. About one and a half squares are filled: roughly 73 million shares, one for each child under 18 in the United States.]

1.5 of 100

of the about 4.8 billion SpaceX shares Musk owns: one each for about 73 million children. [4][5]

the gift

The two grids count different things: every Anthropic share, and the SpaceX shares Musk owns.

The record

### In their words, October 18 to 21.

#### Anthropic

Post, “Investing in the public benefit,” Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026

> Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic's shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board's discretion for every 50% increase in the company's value above a set baseline. [1]

> Anthropic says it might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations. [1]

> AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers. [1]

Post on its Long-Term Benefit Trust, Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026

> Subject to stockholder approval, we've also committed to setting aside a portion of Anthropic's shares to Anthropic Public Benefit Fund. [2]

**More from Anthropic's post**

**The form:** the Fund is a new wholly owned entity, set up as an LLC to give adjustability between different forms of giving. [1]

**Politics:** None of the Anthropic equity held by the LLC will be used for lobbying or political giving, in the US or abroad. [1]

**Work and jobs:** Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. [1]

**Earlier pledges:** our co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings; employees can pledge equity which Anthropic matches. Approximately half of our employees participate in this program. Together with the Fund, roughly 20% of Anthropic shares will be dedicated to the public good. [1]

**Pay:** It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit. [1]

#### Elon Musk

Posts on X, Monday, Oct. 19, 2026

> Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many. [3][8]

> In reply to Anthropic's post (Oct. 18 or 19): I recommend giving the shares directly to the public. [4][5]

Musk did not provide further details on how his share pledge will be carried out. [4] SpaceX closed at $146.03 the Friday before, which puts one share for each of about 73 million children at about $10.7 billion. [4]

Brad Gerstner, on CNBC, Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026

> Gerstner, the Altimeter Capital chief and an architect of Trump Accounts, said the stock donations would come via Trump Accounts, and: Elon is the tip of the iceberg. [6]

**More from the record**

**His stake:** Musk currently owns about 4.8 billion SpaceX shares, according to an August SEC filing. [5]

**Gerstner, Oct. 19:** he suggested in a post on X that the SpaceX shares could be distributed via Trump accounts. [5]

**The Treasury Secretary,** Scott Bessent, on X, Oct. 19: As @TrumpAccounts continues to grow we look forward to more philanthropists joining the movement and helping children across America jumpstart their financial future. [6]

**The President,** on social media, Oct. 19: A BIG THANK YOU to our legendary friend, @ElonMusk, for his incredible generosity in giving SpaceX Stock to millions of American children through TRUMP ACCOUNTS! [8]

**Earlier:** SpaceX President and COO Gwynne Shotwell, with her husband, planned to give money to 2 million children in low-income areas, especially in Texas. [8]

**In Ohio:** Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, on X, Oct. 20, called a proposal to open Trump Accounts to citizens under 40 a game-changer and said he would lead the bill in the Senate to make it happen. That change would take an act of Congress. [6]

The two pledges

### What each commits, who decides, what comes first, and what is not known.

**Anthropic** Oct. 18, 2026

1. #### The pledge **5% of Anthropic's shares** to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, an LLC the company wholly owns; 2% more for every 50% rise in the company's value above a set baseline. [1]
2. #### Who decides **Stockholders** approve the 5%. **The board** adds each 2% at the board's discretion. Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust has the authority to appoint a majority of Anthropic's board. [1][2]
3. #### What has to happen first **A stockholder vote.** Anthropic also says it will share the Fund's structure and governance in the coming months. [1]
4. #### What is not known
   - The date of the vote
   - The baseline, yet to be disclosed [5]
   - Who runs the Fund
   - Which nonprofits or specific populations
   - The date of the first gift

**Elon Musk** Oct. 19, 2026

1. #### The pledge **One of his SpaceX shares** to every kid in America, next year. About 73 million children; about $10.7 billion at $146.03 a share. [3][4]
2. #### Who decides **Musk.** The shares are his own. Through Trump Accounts, a government or nonprofit donor and the Treasury would sign an agreement setting which children receive it. [5][7]
3. #### What has to happen first **A way to deliver it.** The President posted Oct. 19 that the gift goes through TRUMP ACCOUNTS! Gerstner said Oct. 21 the donations would come via Trump Accounts. Musk gave no further details. [4][6][8]
4. #### What is not known
   - How the shares move [4][5]
   - Which donor would hold them first
   - Which children count, and as of what day
   - The date, next year

How it works

### A fund inside a company, and a share in a child's account.

#### Anthropic's Fund

Shares move into an LLC that Anthropic owns; the LLC could give. [1]

1. 1 **Anthropic's shares** Anthropic is a Public Benefit Corporation, which means we're structured to balance commercial growth with our public benefit purpose. [2]
2. 2 **A stockholder vote**The 5% is committed subject to stockholder approval. [1]
3. 3 **The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, an LLC** Rather than a 501(c)(3) or other format. No lobbying or political giving with its Anthropic equity. [1]
4. 4 **Where it could go** Large donations to traditional nonprofits Direct distributions to specific populations

**Dashed:** added at the board's discretion. The 5% and each 2% step are Anthropic's own figures; the baseline is yet to be disclosed. [1][5]

#### A share in a Trump Account

If the gift goes through Trump Accounts, as the President posted and Gerstner said, the Treasury's rules of Sept. 30 set the path. [6][7][8]

[Chart: A drawn account card: a Trump Account for one child, holding 1 share of SpaceX stock, held for 5 years, or until the end of the year the child turns 17 if that comes first.]

1. 1 **Musk's SpaceX shares**About 4.8 billion, by an August filing. [5]
2. 2 **An eligible donor** An eligible donor is a government or nonprofit: a government, a tribal government or a 501(c)(3) organization. [7]
3. 3 **A Treasury acceptance agreement**It sets which children receive the gift: every child with an account, or those in named states or birth years (a class drawn that way needs at least 5,000 children). The stock must be publicly traded stock of a domestic corporation. [7]
4. 4 **Each child's account**The Treasury makes the contribution in an equal amount for each account beneficiary. The accounts are open to any U.S. child under 18 with a Social Security number. [6][7]
5. 5 **Held**Until the earlier of 5 years after it arrives or Dec. 31 of the year the child turns 17. [7]

The rules count a contribution as made when it is received by the Trump account, and not when the contribution is announced. [7]

The timeline

### From the first post to the first share.

on the record still to come, order not known · Sources: [1][3][6][7][8]
